lead_en: Music is sound that people have shaped. This series starts with a single vibrating string and climbs, one question at a time, to scales, instruments, and the music of many places.
lead_zh: 音樂是人把聲音一點一點塑造出來的東西。這個系列從一根振動的弦講起，一次回答一個問題，一路講到音階、樂器，以及各地的音樂。

intro.en: Every lesson has a model you can touch and a sound you can make yourself. All of the sounds are made by your browser, one tone at a time, so there are no recordings and nothing to download.
intro.zh: 每一課都有可以動手的模型，和你自己能發出的聲音。所有的聲音都由瀏覽器一個音一個音合成，沒有任何錄音，也不需要下載。

intro.en: Music words come from many languages. Where a term comes from Italian, you will see the Italian word beside the English and Chinese. Please start with the volume low: the series starts quiet and you can turn it up.
intro.zh: 音樂的詞彙來自很多種語言。有義大利文來源的術語，會把義大利文和英文、中文並列。請先把音量調小：系列的聲音一開始很小聲，你可以再慢慢調大。

units.blurb_en: Pitch, tone color, beat, and the words for loud and fast: the four things you notice first when you listen to any music.
units.blurb_zh: 音高、音色、拍子，以及形容大聲小聲、快慢的詞：聽任何一段音樂時，最先注意到的四件事。

lessons.title: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
lessons.title_zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
lessons.blurb_en: Slide the bridge of a one-string instrument and watch the string shake faster or slower while you hear the note change. Find out why half a string sounds exactly one octave higher.
lessons.blurb_zh: 推動單弦琴的琴橋，看弦振動變快、變慢，同時聽音高改變。再看看為什麼弦短一半，音剛好高一個八度。
lessons.big_idea_en: A note is high when its string shakes fast and low when it shakes slowly. Cut the vibrating part of a string to half its length and it shakes twice as fast, so the note rises by one octave.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 弦振動得快，音就高；振動得慢，音就低。把會振動的那一段縮短一半，振動就快一倍，音剛好高一個八度。

lab.how_en: Drag the gold bridge along the box, or use the slider, and the string gets shorter or longer. Only the part between the bridge and the right end can shake, so that is the part that sets the note. Press Pluck to hear it. The whole string is middle C. The shaking is slowed down on purpose, because the real string shakes far too fast to see.
lab.how_zh: 沿著箱子拖動金色的琴橋，或用滑桿，弦就會變短或變長。只有琴橋到右端那一段能振動，音高就由這一段決定。按「撥弦」就能聽到。整根弦是中央 C。畫面中的振動是刻意放慢的，因為真正的弦振動得太快，眼睛看不到。

legend.en: The part that vibrates and makes the note
legend.zh: 會振動、決定音高的那一段

legend.en: The part that is held still and stays silent
legend.zh: 被壓住不動、不發聲的那一段
刻度：整根、四分之三、三分之二、二分之一、四分之一

lab.scale_en: The model string is about 60 cm long, and one unit in the model is about 7 cm. The vibration is slowed down about 174 times.
lab.scale_zh: 模型裡的弦約 60 公分長，模型中的一個單位約 7 公分；振動畫面放慢了約 174 倍。
lab.credit_html: All sounds on this page are made by your browser, tone by tone. There are no recordings. · 本頁所有的聲音都由瀏覽器即時合成，沒有任何錄音。

paras: Stretch a rubber band around a shoebox and pluck it. You hear a note, and if you touch the band lightly, you can feel it shaking. Now press the band against the box with one finger, so that only half of it is free to move, and pluck it again. The note sounds higher. The rubber band is the same and your pluck is the same. Only one thing has changed: how much of the band can shake.

Musicians call how high or low a note sounds its pitch. Pitch depends on how fast something vibrates, which means how many times it shakes back and forth in one second. That number is called the frequency, and it is measured in hertz (Hz). One hertz is one vibration per second. The faster the vibration, the higher the pitch. The unit is named after the German physicist Heinrich Hertz.

Be careful not to mix up pitch and loudness. A big, strong shake makes a loud sound, while a fast shake makes a high sound. These are two different things. A string can swing widely but slowly, which gives a loud, low note. It can also swing only a little but very quickly, which gives a quiet, high note.

On a string instrument, the length of the part that vibrates helps decide the pitch. If two strings are made of the same material and are equally tight, the shorter one vibrates faster, so it sounds higher. A violin player presses a finger on a string, and this makes the part that can shake shorter. The double bass has longer strings than the other instruments of the violin family, and its notes are very low.

There is a neat rule behind this. When the string is the same, the frequency goes up exactly as the length of the vibrating part goes down. Half the length gives twice the frequency. A note with exactly double the frequency sounds like the same note, only higher, and musicians call the gap between the two notes an octave. In our model, the whole string vibrates 261.63 times every second. Press it at the middle and the frequency is 523.25 Hz. The two notes are C4 and C5, one octave apart.

Other simple fractions work too. Two thirds of the string makes a note that forms a musical fifth with the whole string, and three quarters makes a fourth. The ancient Greeks studied these whole-number ratios on a one-string instrument called a monochord. A modern piano is tuned a little differently, though. It divides every octave into twelve equal steps, so its notes come very close to these simple ratios but are not exactly the same. For two thirds of a string, the difference is only about two cents, and a cent is one hundredth of a piano step. Your ear can hardly tell, but the numbers can.
paras_zh: 把一條橡皮筋套在鞋盒上撥一下，你會聽到一個音；輕輕碰著橡皮筋，還能感覺到它在抖動。現在用一根手指把橡皮筋壓在盒子上，讓只剩一半能自由活動，再撥一次，音變高了。橡皮筋沒換，撥的力氣也一樣，只有一件事不同：能振動的部分有多長。
音樂家把一個音聽起來有多高或多低，叫做「音高」。音高取決於東西振動得多快，也就是一秒鐘來回抖動幾次。這個次數叫「頻率」，單位是「赫茲」（Hz）。一赫茲就是每秒振動一次。振動越快，音高越高。這個單位是以德國物理學家海因里希・赫茲（Heinrich Hertz）命名的。
要小心，不要把音高和音量搞混。大力、大幅度的抖動讓聲音大，快速的抖動讓聲音高，這是兩回事。一根弦可以擺得很寬但很慢，發出又大聲又低的音；也可以只擺一點點但很快，發出小聲又高的音。
在弦樂器上，會振動的那一段有多長，會影響音高。如果兩根弦的材料相同、拉得一樣緊，短的那一根振動得比較快，所以音比較高。小提琴手用手指按住一根弦，就是讓能振動的那一段變短。低音大提琴的弦比提琴家族的其他樂器長，音非常低。
這背後有一條簡單的規則：同樣的弦，會振動的那一段變短多少，頻率就等比例變高。長度一半，頻率就是兩倍。頻率剛好是兩倍的音，聽起來像同一個音、只是更高，音樂家把這兩個音的距離叫「八度」。在我們的模型裡，整根弦每秒振動 261.63 次；在正中間按住，頻率就變成 523.25 赫。這兩個音是 C4 和 C5，相差一個八度。
其他簡單的分數也行得通。弦長的三分之二發出的音，和整根弦構成音樂上的「五度」；四分之三則構成「四度」。古希臘人在一種叫「單弦琴」（monochord）的樂器上研究這些整數比。不過現代鋼琴的調法稍有不同：它把每個八度分成十二個相等的階梯，所以鋼琴的音很接近這些簡單比例，卻不完全一樣。弦長三分之二的音，差距只有大約兩音分；一音分是鋼琴一個階梯的百分之一。耳朵幾乎聽不出來，數字卻看得出來。
questions: How can you make a rubber band sound higher without changing the band?
Why can't we see a guitar string shake 261 times a second, and what does the model do about it?
A friend says, "The higher note must be the louder note." What would you say?
answers: Make the part that can shake shorter, for example by pressing a finger on it, or stretch the band tighter. The shorter or tighter band vibrates faster, so the pitch is higher.

It shakes too fast for our eyes. The model slows the shaking down about 174 times, so the whole string shakes 1.5 times per second and the other lengths are slowed by the same amount. That way you can still see which one is faster.
Pitch and loudness are different. Pitch depends on how fast the string vibrates. Loudness depends on how big the vibration is. A quiet note can be high, and a loud note can be low.

vocab.ex: A guitar string vibrates when you pluck it.
vocab.exzh: 吉他弦一撥就會振動。

vocab.ex: A flute plays notes with a higher pitch than a tuba.
vocab.exzh: 長笛的音高比低音號高。

vocab.ex: The frequency of a note tells how many times it vibrates in one second.
vocab.exzh: 一個音的頻率，說的是它一秒鐘振動幾次。

vocab.ex: A tone of 440 hertz vibrates 440 times every second.
vocab.exzh: 440 赫茲的音，每秒振動 440 次。

vocab.ex: The note one octave above 220 Hz has a frequency of 440 Hz.
vocab.exzh: 比 220 赫高一個八度的音，頻率是 440 赫。

vocab.ex: A violin has four strings.
vocab.exzh: 小提琴有四根弦。

vocab.ex: Play the first note again, a little more slowly.
vocab.exzh: 把第一個音再彈一次，彈慢一點。

vocab.ex: A ratio of 2 to 1 means that one thing is twice as big as the other.
vocab.exzh: 二比一的比例，是說一個東西是另一個的兩倍大。

quiz.q: What do we call how high or low a note sounds?
A string starts to vibrate twice as fast. What happens to the note?
A string vibrates 440 times every second. How do we write its frequency?
You press a string so that the part that can shake is half as long. Compared with the whole string, the frequency is…
Which two notes are exactly one octave apart?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch the bridge slide toward the right. The string gets shorter, shakes faster, and the note climbs.
parts.text_zh: 看琴橋慢慢往右推。弦變短、振動變快，音一路往上爬。

parts.en: Half the string, one octave up
parts.text_en: Pluck the whole string, then half of it. Check the numbers: the second is exactly double the first.
parts.text_zh: 先撥整根弦，再撥一半的弦。核對一下數字：第二個剛好是第一個的兩倍。

parts.meta_en: Close to the piano, not the same
parts.text_en: Simple fractions give notes that come close to piano keys. Read the little difference in cents.
parts.text_zh: 簡單的分數會得到很接近鋼琴琴鍵的音。讀一讀那一點點差距（單位是音分）。

parts.text_en: A real string shakes too fast to see. See how the model slows it down and keeps the speeds in the right proportion.
parts.text_zh: 真正的弦快到看不見。看看模型怎麼把它放慢，又讓快慢的比例保持正確。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Where on the box is the note exactly twice as high as the whole string?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。在箱子的哪個位置，音剛好是整根弦的兩倍高？

higher.lead_en: Eight questions. Each one plays two notes, one after the other. Choose the higher one. The game counts the questions you get right on the first try. Later questions are harder because the two notes are closer together.
higher.lead_zh: 八道題。每一題會連續播兩個音，選出比較高的那一個。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。越後面的題目，兩個音靠得越近，所以越難。

keys.lead_en: Press any key and read its frequency. Then press the key with the same letter, one octave higher: the keys at the two ends are both C. Divide one frequency by the other. What do you notice? You can also use the letter keys on your computer keyboard.
keys.lead_zh: 按任何一個琴鍵，讀出它的頻率。再按高一個八度、字母相同的那個鍵：鍵盤兩端的兩個鍵都是 C。把一個頻率除以另一個，你發現了什麼？也可以用電腦鍵盤上的字母鍵彈。

range.en: How Low and How High Can You Hear?
range.lead_en: People can usually hear frequencies from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, and the range varies from person to person. A piano covers only a part of it. Keep the volume low, then press and hold the button to listen. The tone stops by itself after three seconds.
range.lead_zh: 一般人聽得到的頻率大約從 20 赫到 20,000 赫，每個人不太一樣。鋼琴只涵蓋其中一部分。把音量調小，再按住按鈕聆聽，三秒後聲音會自動停止。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The arts curriculum for music does not use the words pitch or frequency. These entries are the closest ones. The links to pitch are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 藝術領域的音樂課綱沒有出現「音高」或「頻率」這兩個詞。下面是最接近的條目；它們和音高的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 音樂元素，如：節奏、力度、速度等。
items.note_en: Pitch is one of the elements of music. The examples in this entry do not name it.
items.note_zh: 音高是音樂元素之一，但這一條的例示沒有點名音高。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 聲音有大小、高低與音色等不同性質，生活中聲音有樂音與噪音之分，噪音可以防治。
items.note_en: Science class says 高低 (high and low), and its notes also say 音調. Music class says 音高. They name the same thing.
items.note_zh: 自然課綱寫「高低」，說明裡也寫「音調」；音樂課說「音高」，指的是同一件事。

items.area: 自然科學領域・學習內容說明
items.text: 可藉由樂器的演奏，例如：直笛的吹奏、木琴的敲打、烏克麗麗的撥彈或是自製樂器，例如：吸管笛、敲水杯、橡皮筋古箏等活動，了解樂器的發生構造與原理。包含振動部位的判斷、音箱的功用、音調的控制、音色的差異等。
items.note_en: The two classroom activities below, a rubber-band guitar and tapping water cups, come from this suggestion.
items.note_zh: 下面兩個課堂活動——橡皮筋琴與敲水杯——就取自這一段的建議。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國中）
items.text: 樂器的構造、發音原理、演奏技巧，以及不同的演奏形式。
items.note_en: This lesson looks ahead to Lessons 9 and 10, about how instruments make sound.
items.note_zh: 這一課預告了第九、十課：樂器怎麼發出聲音。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音高背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A legend, a one-string instrument, a pitch standard, and a prince
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個傳說、一把單弦琴、一個標準音，和一位王子
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people learned to measure and agree on pitch.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼量出音高、又怎麼對音高取得共識的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: A famous story says that Pythagoras walked past a blacksmith's shop, heard the hammers ring with pleasing notes, and found that their weights were in simple ratios. The oldest full version we have was written down in the first or second century AD. It cannot be true as told, because hammers do not make notes in proportion to their weight. The simple ratios are real, but they belong to string lengths.
cards.body_zh: 有個有名的故事說，畢達哥拉斯經過鐵匠鋪，聽到鐵錘敲出好聽的音，發現鐵錘的重量成簡單的比例。我們看得到最早的完整版本，是西元一、二世紀寫下來的。照故事那樣講是不可能的，因為鐵錘敲出的音高並不和重量成比例。簡單的整數比是真的，但它們屬於弦的長度。

cards.body_en: A monochord is a single string stretched over a box with a movable bridge, very much like our model. The Greeks used it to measure the musical concords. Their results were whole-number ratios: the octave is 2 to 1, the fifth is 3 to 2, and the fourth is 4 to 3. The movable bridge is the same idea as your finger on a violin string.
cards.body_zh: 單弦琴是在箱子上拉一根弦、再加一個可以移動的琴橋，和我們的模型很像。希臘人用它來量音樂上的「協和音程」，得到的是整數比：八度是 2 比 1、五度是 3 比 2、四度是 4 比 3。可移動的琴橋，和你的手指按在小提琴弦上是同一個道理。

cards.zh: 為什麼標準音是 440 赫
cards.body_en: Pitch used to be different from place to place and from century to century. A law passed in France on February 16, 1859, set the A above middle C at 435 Hz. In May 1939, delegates met at Broadcasting House in London and agreed on 440 Hz. The International Organization for Standardization took it up as a recommendation in 1955 and formalized it as ISO 16 in 1975. Even now not every orchestra follows it.
cards.body_zh: 過去各地、各個世紀的音高都不一樣。法國在 1859 年 2 月 16 日通過法律，把中央 C 上面的 A 定為 435 赫。1939 年 5 月，各國代表在倫敦的 BBC 廣播大樓開會，同意採用 440 赫。國際標準化組織（ISO）在 1955 年把它當作建議採用，1975 年正式定為 ISO 16。直到現在，也不是每個樂團都照著用。

cards.body_en: Zhu Zaiyu was a prince of the Ming dynasty who spent thirty years on the mathematics of tuning. In 1584 he described equal temperament: each of the twelve steps in an octave multiplies the frequency by the same number, about 1.0595. Some people think his work may have reached Europe, but there is no evidence for that. Equal temperament has been the main tuning system of Western music since the twentieth century.
cards.body_zh: 朱載堉是明朝的王子，花了三十年研究調音的數學。1584 年，他說明了十二平均律：一個八度裡的十二個階梯，每一階都乘上同一個數，大約是 1.0595。有人認為他的研究可能傳到了歐洲，但沒有證據。二十世紀以來，十二平均律是西方音樂最主要的調音系統。

myths.myth_en: A higher note is a louder note.
myths.myth_zh: 音越高，就越大聲。
myths.fact_en: Pitch and loudness are different properties of a sound. Pitch depends on how fast something vibrates. Loudness depends on how strongly it vibrates. A tiny, fast shake gives a quiet, high note.
myths.fact_zh: 音高和音量是聲音不同的性質。音高看振動得多快，音量看振動得多用力。很小、很快的抖動，會發出小聲又高的音。

myths.myth_en: Pythagoras found the notes by listening to blacksmiths' hammers.
myths.myth_zh: 畢達哥拉斯是聽鐵匠敲鐵錘才發現音階的。
myths.fact_en: The story is a legend, and it would not work: the pitch of a hammer is not proportional to its weight. The simple ratios are real for strings, and the Greeks studied them on a monochord.
myths.fact_zh: 這是傳說，而且照故事那樣做行不通：鐵錘敲出的音高和重量並不成比例。簡單的整數比在弦上是真的，希臘人就是用單弦琴研究它們。

myths.myth_en: Two thirds of a string gives exactly the note you find on a piano.
myths.myth_zh: 弦長三分之二，剛好就是鋼琴上那個音。
myths.fact_en: It is very close, but not exact. Two thirds of a C4 string gives 392.44 Hz, and the piano's G4 is 391.99 Hz, about two cents lower. The piano splits the octave into twelve equal steps instead.
myths.fact_zh: 非常接近，但不完全一樣。C4 的弦取三分之二，得到 392.44 赫；鋼琴的 G4 是 391.99 赫，低了大約兩音分。鋼琴是把八度分成十二個相等的階梯。

myths.myth_en: If something shakes, you can always hear it.
myths.myth_zh: 只要東西在抖，你就一定聽得到。
myths.fact_en: People hear frequencies from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Vibrations below 20 Hz are called infrasound, and those above 20,000 Hz are called ultrasound. We cannot hear them, although some animals can.
myths.fact_zh: 人聽得到的頻率大約是 20 赫到 20,000 赫。低於 20 赫叫次聲波，高於 20,000 赫叫超聲波；我們聽不見，有些動物卻聽得見。

tricks.body_en: Slow shake, low note. Pitch follows the speed of the vibration.
tricks.body_zh: 抖得慢，音就低。音高跟著振動的快慢走。

tricks.title_en: Half the string, one octave up
tricks.body_en: Half the length, double the frequency.
tricks.body_zh: 長度一半，頻率兩倍。

tricks.title_en: Double the hertz, same note, higher
tricks.body_en: 220 Hz, 440 Hz, 880 Hz: each is the same note, one octave up.
tricks.body_zh: 220 赫、440 赫、880 赫：每個都是同名的音，一個比一個高八度。

tricks.title_en: Pitch is speed; volume is size
tricks.title_zh: 音高看快慢，音量看大小
tricks.body_en: How fast the string shakes sets the pitch. How far it swings sets the volume.
tricks.body_zh: 弦抖得多快決定音高，擺得多遠決定音量。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%. Never begin with the volume at maximum.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。千萬不要一開始就把音量開到最大。

safety.en: With headphones, set a comfortable volume in a quiet place and keep it to no more than 60% of maximum. The World Health Organization also suggests using personal audio devices for less than one hour a day.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，在安靜的地方調到舒適的音量，不要超過最大音量的 60%。世界衛生組織也建議，每天使用個人音響裝置的時間少於一小時。

safety.en: The World Health Organization recommends a safe level of 80 decibels for 40 hours a week, and the louder the sound, the shorter the safe time. Music through headphones at full volume is about 94 to 110 decibels.
safety.zh: 世界衛生組織建議的安全聆聽量是每週 40 小時、80 分貝；聲音越大，安全的時間越短。耳機開到最大音量的音樂，大約是 94 到 110 分貝。

safety.en: Do not put your ear against a speaker or hold a high tone for a long time. The hearing-range slider plays for three seconds at most and is kept quiet on purpose. If a sound hurts, stop and turn the volume down.
safety.zh: 不要把耳朵貼在喇叭上，也不要長時間聽很高的音。聽力範圍的滑桿最多只播三秒，而且刻意壓得很小聲。如果聲音讓你不舒服，就停下來、把音量調小。

materials.en: An open box, such as a tissue box with no lid, or a shoebox
materials.zh: 一個沒有蓋子的盒子，例如面紙盒或鞋盒

materials.en: Three rubber bands of the same thickness
A pencil to use as a bridge, and a ruler
materials.zh: 一支當琴橋的鉛筆，和一把尺

materials.en: Safety glasses, or keep your face to the side
materials.zh: 護目鏡，或把臉轉到旁邊

steps.en: Stretch the three rubber bands around the box, a few centimeters apart. Slide the pencil under them at one end to make a bridge.
steps.zh: 把三條橡皮筋套在盒子上，彼此隔幾公分。在一端把鉛筆塞到橡皮筋底下，當作琴橋。

steps.en: Pluck one band and listen. This is your whole string.
steps.zh: 撥一條橡皮筋，聽聽看。這就是你的「整根弦」。

steps.en: Press the band against the box at its middle with one finger and pluck the free half. Is the note higher or lower?
steps.zh: 用一根手指把橡皮筋在正中間壓在盒子上，撥另一半。音變高還是變低？

steps.en: Measure the part that can shake with the ruler. Try a half and three quarters. Write down the length and whether the note is higher or lower.
steps.zh: 用尺量出會振動的那一段。試試一半和四分之三。記下長度，以及音是比較高還是比較低。

steps.en: Now change one more thing: pull one band tighter. Does the pitch go up or down? Change only one thing at a time.
steps.zh: 再改變另一件事：把一條橡皮筋拉得更緊。音高是升還是降？一次只改變一件事。

activities.tip_en: A shorter band and a tighter band both sound higher. Our model keeps the tension fixed, so that only the length changes. Do not stretch a band until it snaps, because it can fly back at your face.
activities.tip_zh: 橡皮筋變短、或拉得更緊，音都會變高。我們的模型固定張力，只改變長度。不要把橡皮筋拉到快斷，它彈回來可能打到臉。

materials.en: Five identical plastic cups (plastic is safer than glass)
materials.zh: 五個一模一樣的塑膠杯（塑膠比玻璃安全）

materials.en: Water and a spoon
A marker and a sheet of paper for your table
materials.zh: 一支簽字筆和一張記錄用的紙

steps.en: Line up the cups. Pour a different amount of water into each one, from almost empty to almost full.
steps.zh: 把杯子排成一排，每個杯子倒入不一樣多的水，從幾乎沒有到幾乎滿。

steps.en: Tap each cup lightly with the spoon. Which one sounds highest, and which sounds lowest?
steps.zh: 用湯匙輕輕敲每個杯子。哪一個最高、哪一個最低？

steps.en: Put the cups in order from the lowest note to the highest. Write the order on your paper.
steps.zh: 把杯子照音高從低到高排好，把順序寫在紙上。

steps.en: Predict first, then test: if you blow across the top of a bottle with water in it instead of tapping, will the order stay the same?
steps.zh: 先預測，再測試：如果不用敲的，改成對著裝了水的瓶口吹氣，順序會不會一樣？

activities.tip_en: Tapping makes the cup and the water vibrate. Blowing across a bottle makes the air inside vibrate. Different things vibrate, so the order of the notes can change. Which part is shaking in each case?
activities.tip_zh: 敲的時候，是杯子和水在振動；對著瓶口吹氣，是瓶子裡的空氣在振動。振動的東西不一樣，所以音的順序可能會不同。每一種情況裡，是哪個部分在抖？

links_head.en: Where sound comes from, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 聲音從哪裡來，以及下一課

links.en: How Does Sound Reach Your Ears?
links.note_en: Sound is a vibration that travels through the air. That lesson follows it from the speaker to your ear. This lesson does not repeat it.
links.note_zh: 聲音是一種在空氣中傳遞的振動。那一課從喇叭一路講到你的耳朵；這一課不再重複。

links.en: Why Does a Piano Sound Different from a Violin?
links.zh: 同一個音，鋼琴和小提琴為什麼聽起來不一樣？
links.note_en: Two instruments can play the same pitch and still sound different. The next lesson looks inside a single note.
links.note_zh: 兩種樂器可以彈同一個音高，聽起來卻不一樣。下一課要看進一個音的裡面。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The frequencies and ratios are computed by the page itself and covered by automatic tests.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；頻率與比例由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試。

sources.en: Pitch is the highness or lowness of a sound, set by the frequency of vibration; “pitch” in the Ministry of Education Dictionary, as quoted by the Encyclopedia of Education
sources.zh: 音高：聲音頻率的高低程度，由振動次數決定（教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》，轉載於教育百科）

sources.en: Frequency, the hertz (one cycle per second), and a note one octave higher having double the frequency
sources.zh: 頻率、赫茲（每秒一個週期），以及高一個八度的音頻率加倍

sources.en: The hertz is the SI unit of frequency, named after Heinrich Hertz
sources.zh: 赫茲是 SI 的頻率單位，以海因里希・赫茲命名

sources.en: An octave is an interval between two tones, one having twice the frequency of the other (2:1)
sources.zh: 八度是兩個音之間的音程，其中一個的頻率是另一個的兩倍（2:1）

sources.en: Frequency of a string fixed at both ends goes as 1/(2L): shorter string, higher frequency
sources.zh: 兩端固定的弦，基頻與 1/(2L) 成正比：弦越短，頻率越高

sources.en: Mersenne's laws of strings, first proposed in 1636 in Harmonie universelle (length, tension, and density)
sources.zh: 梅森的弦定律，1636 年首見於《宇宙的和聲》（弦長、張力與線密度）

sources.en: The octave, fifth, and fourth correspond to the ratios 2:1, 3:2, and 4:3; the blacksmith story is false because hammer pitch is not proportional to weight
sources.zh: 八度、五度、四度對應 2:1、3:2、4:3；鐵匠鋪的故事不成立，因為鐵錘的音高與重量不成正比

sources.en: The oldest recorded version of the hammers story is in Nicomachus, first or second century AD
sources.zh: 鐵錘故事現存最早的版本出自尼科馬庫斯，約西元一、二世紀

sources.en: A monochord is a string stretched over a sound box with movable bridges, used to illustrate the mathematics of pitch
sources.zh: 單弦琴是在音箱上拉一根弦、配上可移動的琴橋，用來示範音高的數學關係

sources.en: The Greeks found that the octave, the fourth, and the fifth correspond to whole-number ratios of string length
sources.zh: 希臘人發現八度、四度、五度對應弦長的整數比

sources.en: Equal temperament has been the predominant tuning system of Western music since the 20th century
sources.zh: 二十世紀以來，十二平均律是西方音樂最主要的調音系統

sources.en: A4 = 440 Hz: the 1939 London meeting, ISO Recommendation R 16 in 1955, ISO 16 in 1975; not universally followed
sources.zh: A4＝440 赫：1939 年倫敦會議、1955 年 ISO 建議 R 16、1975 年 ISO 16；並非人人遵守

sources.en: France's law of February 16, 1859, set the A at 435 Hz (the diapason normal)
sources.zh: 法國 1859 年 2 月 16 日的法律把 A 定為 435 赫（diapason normal）

sources.en: Middle C is C4, about 261.626 Hz; scientific pitch notation
sources.zh: 中央 C 是 C4，約 261.626 赫；科學音高記號法

sources.en: An 88-key piano runs from A0 (27.5 Hz) to C8 (4186.009 Hz)
A just perfect fifth is about 701.955 cents; the equal-tempered fifth is 700 cents, about two cents narrower
sources.zh: 純律五度約 701.955 音分；平均律五度 700 音分，窄約兩音分

sources.en: A cent is one hundredth of an equal-tempered semitone; 1200 cents make an octave
sources.zh: 一音分是十二平均律半音的百分之一；一個八度是 1200 音分

sources.en: Zhu Zaiyu, a prince of the Ming dynasty, described equal temperament in 1584
sources.zh: 朱載堉，明朝王子，1584 年說明十二平均律

sources.en: No evidence confirms that Zhu's work was transmitted to Europe
sources.zh: 沒有證據證實朱載堉的著作傳到歐洲

sources.en: Humans hear about 20 Hz to 20 kHz; below 20 Hz is infrasound and above 20 kHz is ultrasound
sources.zh: 人耳聽得到約 20 赫到 20 千赫；低於 20 赫是次聲波、高於 20 千赫是超聲波

sources.en: The human range is commonly given as 20 to 20,000 Hz, with considerable variation between individuals
sources.zh: 人耳範圍一般記為 20 到 20,000 赫，個體差異很大

sources.en: Safe listening: 80 decibels for 40 hours a week; keep headphone volume to 60% of maximum; personal audio devices less than one hour a day
sources.zh: 安全聆聽：每週 40 小時、80 分貝；耳機音量不超過最大的 60%；個人音響裝置每天少於一小時

sources.en: Sounds at or above 85 dBA can cause hearing loss with long or repeated exposure; typical levels of familiar sounds
sources.zh: 長時間或反覆暴露在 85 分貝（A 加權）以上的聲音會造成聽力損失；常見聲音的分貝

sources.en: Chinese terms: pitch 音高 (music), frequency 頻率, hertz 赫[茲], octave 八[音]度, monochord 單弦
sources.zh: 中文名詞：pitch 音高（音樂）、frequency 頻率、hertz 赫[茲]、octave 八[音]度、monochord 單弦
sources.src: 國家教育研究院「學術名詞資訊網」

sources.zh: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要藝術領域：音 E-Ⅱ-4、音 E-Ⅳ-2
sources.src: 國家教育研究院，十二年國教藝術領域課綱

sources.zh: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要自然科學領域：INe-Ⅲ-6 與學習內容說明（橡皮筋古箏、敲水杯）

lessons.title: Why Does a Piano Sound Different from a Violin?
lessons.title_zh: 同一個音，鋼琴和小提琴為什麼聽起來不一樣？
lessons.blurb_en: Pluck a string in the middle or near the end and watch it shake in many ways at once. Then mix the harmonics yourself and hear how the same note changes its color.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在弦的中間或靠近一端撥一下，看它同時用很多種方式振動。再自己混合諧波，聽同一個音怎麼換了顏色。
lessons.big_idea_en: A note is not one shake but a mix of many shakes at once: the fundamental and its harmonics. The pitch you hear comes from the fundamental. Which harmonics are strong, and how the note begins and fades, give it its tone color.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 一個音不是只有一種振動，而是很多種振動同時混在一起：基音和它的諧波。你聽到的音高來自基音；哪些諧波強、這個音怎麼開始又怎麼消失，決定了它的音色。

lab.title_zh: 一根弦，同時很多種振動
lab.how_en: The string is C4, 261.63 Hz. Click the box to pluck the string at that spot, or use the slider. Above the string, each thin line is one way of shaking: harmonic 1 is the whole string, harmonic 2 is two halves, harmonic 3 is three thirds, and so on. The gold string at the bottom is all of them added together, and that is the sound. White dots mark the nodes, the points that stay still. The shaking is slowed down on purpose.
lab.how_zh: 這根弦是 C4，261.63 赫。點箱子，就在那裡撥弦；也可以用滑桿。弦的上方，每一條細線是一種振動方式：第 1 諧波是整根弦、第 2 諧波是兩個半根、第 3 諧波是三個三分之一，依此類推。最下面金色的弦是全部加起來的樣子，也就是你聽到的聲音。白點標出節點，就是不動的點。振動畫面是刻意放慢的。

legend.en: The string you hear: all the harmonics added together
legend.zh: 你聽到的弦：所有諧波加起來

legend.en: One thin line for each harmonic, with its frequency
legend.zh: 每個諧波一條細線，附上頻率

legend.en: White dots: nodes, the points that do not move

lab.scale_en: The model string is about 60 cm long. The fundamental shakes once per second here, slowed down about 262 times, and harmonic n shakes n times per second.
lab.scale_zh: 模型裡的弦約 60 公分長。基音在這裡每秒振動一次，放慢了大約 262 倍；第 n 諧波每秒 n 次。
lab.credit_html: All sounds on this page are made by your browser, tone by tone. They are simple mixes of harmonics, not recordings of a piano or a violin. · 本頁所有的聲音都由瀏覽器即時合成，是簡單的諧波混合，不是鋼琴或小提琴的錄音。

paras: Play middle C on a piano, and then play the same note on a violin. The pitch is the same. The loudness can be the same too. Yet you would never mix them up, even with your eyes closed. Something about the sound is different. Musicians call it tone color, or timbre (say "TAM-ber").

A well-known standard from the American National Standards Institute describes timbre as the quality that lets a listener tell that two sounds are different, even when they have the same loudness and the same pitch. So timbre is not pitch, and it is not loudness. It is the third thing.

To see where timbre comes from, look inside one note. A string does not shake in only one way. It shakes as a whole, and at the same time in two halves, in three thirds, and so on. Each way of shaking is called a harmonic. The whole-string shake is the fundamental, or the first harmonic. The second harmonic has exactly twice the frequency, and the third has three times, and so on. The second harmonic is also called the first overtone.

You do not hear these harmonics as separate notes. You hear one note, and its pitch is the fundamental. But the mix matters. If the harmonics are strong, the sound is bright and buzzy. If only a few are present, the sound is round and soft. The mix of harmonics changes the shape of the sound wave, even though the repeating rate, and so the pitch, stays the same.

Where does the mix come from? Partly from how you start the string. Helmholtz, a German scientist who wrote a famous book on sound in 1863, noticed that a string struck in its middle loses its second partial tone. In the model you can check this: pluck exactly in the middle and every even harmonic disappears, because a node sits right where you pluck. Pluck near the end and many high harmonics are strong. Partly it comes from the instrument itself. A clarinet, for example, mostly makes the odd harmonics.

Time matters too. A piano string is struck by a hammer, so the note starts at once and then fades. A bowed violin string can start more gently and keep going. Reference works on timbre note that if you remove the beginning of a piano or trumpet note, it becomes harder to tell which instrument it is. Our model uses only simple recipes, so it cannot sound like a real piano or violin. Real instruments have many more harmonics and many more details.
paras_zh: 在鋼琴上彈中央 C，再在小提琴上拉同一個音。音高一樣，音量也可以一樣。可是就算閉著眼睛，你也不會把它們搞混。聲音裡有某個地方不一樣。音樂家把它叫做「音色」，英文是 tone color 或 timbre（唸成「坦伯」）。
美國國家標準學會有一份很有名的標準，把音色描述成：就算兩個聲音的響度和音高都一樣，聽的人還是能分辨它們不同的那種性質。所以音色不是音高，也不是音量，它是第三件事。
要看出音色從哪裡來，得看進一個音的裡面。一根弦不是只有一種振動方式。它整根在振動，同時也一半一半地振動、三分之一三分之一地振動，依此類推。每一種振動方式叫一個「諧波」。整根弦的振動是「基音」，也就是第一諧波；第二諧波的頻率剛好是兩倍，第三諧波是三倍，依此類推。第二諧波也叫做第一泛音。
你不會把這些諧波聽成一個個分開的音。你聽到的是一個音，音高就是基音。但是混合的比例很重要：諧波強，聲音就明亮、有點嗡嗡的；只有幾個諧波，聲音就圓潤柔和。諧波的混合會改變聲波的形狀，可是重複的快慢不變，所以音高也不變。
這個混合從哪裡來？一部分來自你怎麼讓弦動起來。亥姆霍茲是一位德國科學家，1863 年寫了一本關於聲音的名著，他發現弦在正中間被敲時，第二個分音就消失了。你可以在模型裡檢查：剛好在正中間撥，所有偶數諧波都不見了，因為節點剛好在你撥的位置。靠近一端撥，很多高諧波就很強。另一部分來自樂器本身，例如單簧管主要發出奇數諧波。
時間也很重要。鋼琴的弦是被琴槌敲響的，所以聲音一開始就出現，然後慢慢消失；用弓拉的小提琴弦可以輕輕地開始、持續下去。談音色的參考資料提到，如果把鋼琴或小號的音一開始的那一瞬間拿掉，就比較難聽出是哪一種樂器。我們的模型只用簡單的配方，所以不可能聽起來像真的鋼琴或小提琴；真的樂器有多得多的諧波和細節。
questions: Two notes have the same pitch and the same loudness, but they sound different. What do we call that difference?
A note has a fundamental of 200 Hz. What are the frequencies of its first four harmonics?
Why do the even harmonics disappear when you pluck a string exactly in the middle?
answers: It is called timbre, or tone color. Timbre is the quality that tells two sounds apart when their pitch and loudness are the same.
The harmonics are whole-number multiples of the fundamental: 200 Hz, 400 Hz, 600 Hz, and 800 Hz. The first one is the fundamental itself.

Every even harmonic has a node exactly in the middle of the string, a point that does not move. If you pluck right there, those harmonics cannot start. The odd harmonics have their biggest swing in the middle, so they are strong.

vocab.ex: The flute and the oboe play the same note, but their timbre is very different.
vocab.exzh: 長笛和雙簧管吹同一個音，但它們的音色很不一樣。

vocab.ex: The fundamental is the lowest frequency in a note, and it gives the pitch.
vocab.exzh: 基音是一個音裡頻率最低的成分，音高就是它決定的。

vocab.ex: The third harmonic vibrates three times as fast as the fundamental.
vocab.exzh: 第三諧波的振動速度是基音的三倍。

vocab.ex: The first overtone is the second harmonic.
vocab.exzh: 第一泛音就是第二諧波。

vocab.ex: A pure tone has the smooth waveform of a sine wave.
vocab.exzh: 純音的波形是平滑的正弦波。

vocab.ex: A piano has a sharp attack because the hammer hits the string.
vocab.exzh: 鋼琴的起音很尖銳，因為琴槌敲到了弦。

vocab.ex: After you press a piano key, the note slowly decays.
vocab.exzh: 鋼琴鍵按下去以後，聲音慢慢衰減。

vocab.ex: She plucked the string with her finger.
vocab.exzh: 她用手指撥了那根弦。

quiz.q: What is timbre?
options: The quality that tells two sounds apart when pitch and loudness are the same
How high or low a note is

quiz.q: A note has a fundamental of 100 Hz. What is the frequency of its third harmonic?
You pluck a string exactly in its middle. Which harmonics disappear?
Which of these gives a note its timbre?
options: The mix of harmonics and how the note begins and fades
Only the length of the string

quiz.q: A note that has only odd harmonics, fading as 1/n, is made of harmonics…

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.en: One string, many ways to shake
parts.text_en: Watch the harmonics join one at a time. Each one is a new line, and the note gets brighter.
parts.text_zh: 看諧波一個一個加進來。每加一個就多一條線，聲音越來越亮。

parts.text_en: Look at harmonics 2, 4, and 6. A node sits where you pluck, so they cannot start.
parts.text_zh: 看第 2、4、6 諧波。節點剛好在你撥的位置，它們動不起來。

parts.text_en: The same string and the same pitch, but the sound is brighter and thinner.
parts.text_zh: 同一根弦、同一個音高，可是聲音比較亮、比較薄。

parts.zh: 第 2 諧波就是第一課的一半弦長
parts.text_en: Switch off everything except harmonic 2. The string shakes in two halves, the same note you made by pressing a string in lesson 1.
parts.text_zh: 只留第 2 諧波。弦分成兩半各自振動，就是第一課把弦按住一半得到的那個音。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the slider and the switches. Which harmonics are missing when you pluck at one fifth of the string?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試滑桿和開關。在弦長五分之一的地方撥，缺少哪些諧波？

mix.lead_en: Every slider is one harmonic of the note C4, 261.63 Hz. Push a slider up to add that harmonic, and the wave shape changes. The pitch stays the same, but the color changes. Try the four recipes. The names describe the mix, not any real instrument.
mix.lead_zh: 每一根滑桿是 C4（261.63 赫）這個音的一個諧波。把滑桿往上推就加入那個諧波，波形跟著改變。音高不變，顏色卻變了。試試四個配方。名稱描述的是混合的方式，不是哪一種真的樂器。

env.zh: 同樣的混合，不同的開始
env.lead_en: A note also has a shape in time. Attack is how fast it starts, decay is how fast it fades, and sustain is how much is kept. Compare a struck or plucked note, which starts at once and fades, with a bowed note, which starts gently and keeps going. The harmonics are exactly the same in both.
env.lead_zh: 一個音在時間上也有形狀：起音是它多快響起來、衰減是它多快變小聲、維持是它保留多少。比較敲擊或撥奏的音（一開始就響、然後慢慢消失）和拉奏的音（輕輕開始、一直持續）。兩個的諧波完全一樣。

which.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays a note made from one of the four recipes. Choose the picture of the wave that matches. The notes all have the same pitch, so you have to listen for the color.
which.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題播出用四個配方之一做成的音，選出對得上的波形圖。每個音的音高都一樣，所以你要聽的是顏色。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: In the arts curriculum, tone color first appears in junior high school. Elementary grades 3 to 6 do not list it among the elements of music, so for those grades the science curriculum is the closest match. The links to this lesson are our reading.
curric.lead_zh: 藝術領域的課綱裡，「音色」到國中才出現；國小三到六年級的音樂元素沒有列到音色，所以對國小高年級來說，最接近的是自然領域的條目。它們和本課的連結是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國中）
items.text: 音樂元素，如：音色、調式、和聲等。
items.note_en: Tone color is named as an element of music.
items.note_zh: 課綱明白把音色列為音樂元素。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 聲音有大小、高低與音色等不同性質，生活中聲音有樂音與噪音之分，噪音可以防治。
items.note_en: Loudness, pitch, and tone color are three different properties of a sound.
items.note_zh: 音量、音高、音色是聲音三種不同的性質。

items.area: 自然科學領域・學習內容說明
items.text: 可藉由樂器的演奏，例如：直笛的吹奏、木琴的敲打、烏克麗麗的撥彈或是自製樂器，例如：吸管笛、敲水杯、橡皮筋古箏等活動，了解樂器的發生構造與原理。包含振動部位的判斷、音箱的功用、音調的控制、音色的差異等。
items.note_en: The notes name “differences in tone color” as something to learn from playing instruments.
items.note_zh: 說明裡把「音色的差異」列為從演奏樂器中要了解的內容。

items.area: 自然科學領域・國中說明
items.text: 經由自製樂器或樂器表演，知道聲音可由音量、音調及音色來描述。亦可以自由軟體讓學生看到不同樂器的音色和波形的關係。了解弦的鬆緊、空氣柱的長短、鼓的大小如何影響波形。
items.note_en: Seeing the link between tone color and waveform with software is exactly what the mixing sliders on this page do.
items.note_zh: 用軟體看見音色和波形的關係，正是本頁混合滑桿做的事。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind Tone Color · 音色背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A scientist, a tube, a hammer and a bow, and a word
culture_cards.title_zh: 一位科學家、一根管子、一把槌子和一張弓，和一個詞
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people came to understand the color of sound.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼一步步看懂聲音的「顏色」的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: The German scientist Hermann von Helmholtz published a book on the sensations of tone in 1863. In it he studied the partial tones of strings, tubes, and voices. He noted that when a string is struck in its middle, the second partial tone disappears. The English translation by Alexander Ellis appeared in 1875.
cards.body_zh: 德國科學家亥姆霍茲（Hermann von Helmholtz）在 1863 年出版了一本談聽覺與音的名著，書裡研究了弦、管和人聲的分音。他指出，弦在正中間被敲時，第二個分音就消失了。亞歷山大・艾利斯（Alexander Ellis）的英文譯本在 1875 年出版。

cards.body_en: A clarinet is a tube that is almost closed at one end by the reed. Such a tube mostly reinforces the odd harmonics, so a clarinet makes mainly the odd members of the series. The even ones are weak, not completely missing. Helmholtz found the same by ear, up to the seventh partial, and found that instruments with conical tubes, such as the oboe, reinforce all of them.
cards.body_zh: 單簧管是一根一端幾乎被簧片封住的管子。這樣的管子主要加強奇數諧波，所以單簧管主要發出奇數的那幾個；偶數的很弱，但不是完全沒有。亥姆霍茲用耳朵也發現了同樣的事，一直到第七個分音；他還發現雙簧管這類圓錐形管的樂器，會把所有的諧波都加強。

cards.k: A Hammer and a Bow · 一把槌子和一張弓
cards.en: Two ways to start a string
cards.zh: 讓弦動起來的兩種方法
cards.body_en: A piano string is struck by a felt-covered hammer, so the sound begins at once and fades. A bow does something different: the string clings to the bow, is carried along, and then suddenly slips back. This stick-and-slip motion can keep the string going. A piano string is also a little stiff, so its higher partials come out slightly above exact whole-number multiples.
cards.body_zh: 鋼琴的弦是被包著毛氈的琴槌敲響的，所以聲音一開始就出現，然後慢慢消失。弓的做法不一樣：弦黏在弓上被帶著走，然後突然滑回來。這種「黏住、滑開」的運動可以讓弦一直振動下去。鋼琴的弦還有一點硬，所以它的高分音會比剛好的整數倍稍微高一點。

cards.body_en: Helmholtz called it Klangfarbe, German for “tone color,” and English adopted both “tone color” and “timbre.” In Chinese, the dictionary of the Ministry of Education also lists 音品 and 音質 for the same idea. Chinese players use words for it too. The erhu, for example, is described as having a beautiful timbre that ranges from soft to strong.
cards.body_zh: 亥姆霍茲把它叫做 Klangfarbe，德文就是「聲音的顏色」；英文後來用 tone color 和 timbre 兩個詞。在中文裡，教育部辭典把同一個概念也寫作「音品」「音質」。演奏者也用詞彙來形容它，例如二胡被形容為音色優美、表現力強，剛柔多變。

myths.myth_en: Two instruments that play the same note make exactly the same sound wave.
myths.myth_zh: 兩種樂器彈同一個音，發出的聲波一模一樣。
myths.fact_en: They share the same repeating rate, so the same pitch. But the mix of harmonics and the way the note starts and fades are different, so the wave shapes differ.
myths.fact_zh: 它們重複的快慢一樣，所以音高一樣；可是諧波的混合、以及音怎麼開始和消失都不同，所以波形不一樣。

myths.myth_en: You can hear the harmonics as separate notes.
myths.myth_zh: 你可以把諧波一個一個聽成分開的音。
myths.fact_en: Normally you hear one note, and its pitch is the fundamental. The harmonics change the color of that note. It takes practice, or special tools, to pick them out.
myths.fact_zh: 平常你只聽到一個音，音高就是基音；諧波改變的是這個音的顏色。要把它們一個個挑出來，需要練習或特別的工具。

myths.myth_en: A violin's sound is a sawtooth wave.
myths.myth_zh: 小提琴的聲音就是鋸齒波。
myths.fact_en: A bow drives the string with a motion that looks like a sawtooth, and synthesizers use sawtooth waves as one ingredient for bowed sounds. But the sound of a real violin is far more complicated than any simple recipe.
myths.fact_zh: 弓帶動弦的運動看起來像鋸齒，合成器也拿鋸齒波當做拉弦聲音的材料之一；但真的小提琴的聲音，比任何簡單的配方都複雜得多。

myths.myth_en: The beginning of a note does not matter for telling instruments apart.
myths.myth_zh: 要分辨樂器，一個音開頭那一瞬間不重要。
myths.fact_en: It matters a lot. If you remove the attack from a piano or trumpet note, it becomes harder to identify, because the hammer strike or the first blast of breath is very characteristic.
myths.fact_zh: 非常重要。如果把鋼琴或小號的音一開始的那一瞬間拿掉，就比較難辨認，因為槌子敲弦的聲音或第一口氣的聲音，都是那種樂器很有特色的部分。

tricks.body_en: The fundamental sets the pitch. The mix of harmonics sets the color.
tricks.body_zh: 基音決定音高，諧波的混合決定顏色。

tricks.title_zh: 諧波：1 倍、2 倍、3 倍、4 倍
tricks.body_en: Each harmonic is a whole-number multiple of the fundamental.
tricks.body_zh: 每個諧波都是基音頻率的整數倍。

tricks.title_en: Pluck in the middle, lose the evens
tricks.body_en: A node sits where you pluck, so the even harmonics cannot start.
tricks.body_zh: 節點剛好在撥的位置，偶數諧波動不起來。

tricks.title_en: Color is the mix and the start
tricks.body_en: Harmonics, attack, and decay together make a tone color.
tricks.body_zh: 諧波、起音、衰減，合起來才是一個音色。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。

safety.en: The mixes on this page are scaled so that the wave never gets taller than the pure tone. A bright mix with many harmonics can still sound sharp. If it hurts, stop and turn the volume down.
safety.zh: 本頁的混合都會縮放，讓波形不會比純音更高；但諧波很多的明亮混合聽起來還是可能刺耳。如果不舒服，就停下來、把音量調小。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum in a quiet place, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，在安靜的地方不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: In the classroom activities, do not shout or blow into anyone's ear. Sing or hum at a comfortable volume.
safety.zh: 課堂活動中，不要對著別人的耳朵大叫或吹氣。用舒服的音量唱或哼就好。

activities.title_en: Pluck in the Middle, Pluck Near the End
activities.title_zh: 在中間撥，在靠近一端撥

materials.en: The rubber-band box from lesson 1, or a guitar or ukulele if your class has one
materials.zh: 第一課的橡皮筋盒子；班上有吉他或烏克麗麗也可以

materials.en: A ruler
A sheet of paper for words

steps.en: Pluck one string right in its middle. Listen, and write a word for how it sounds: round, bright, hollow, thin, buzzy…
steps.zh: 在弦的正中間撥一下。仔細聽，寫下一個形容它的詞：圓、亮、空、薄、嗡嗡……

steps.en: Pluck the same string about one tenth of the way from the end. Is the pitch the same? Is the color the same?
steps.zh: 在離一端大約十分之一的地方撥同一根弦。音高一樣嗎？顏色一樣嗎？

steps.en: Repeat three times each, and take turns with a partner, who listens with eyes closed and says which one was plucked near the end.
steps.zh: 各重複三次，兩人輪流；另一個人閉著眼睛聽，說出哪一次是靠近一端撥的。

steps.en: Compare with the model: it says that plucking near the end gives more high harmonics.
steps.zh: 和模型比對：模型說，靠近一端撥，高諧波比較多。

activities.tip_en: The difference is small on a rubber band, so listen carefully and try more than once. If your partner cannot tell, that is a result too. Keep the rubber band away from your face.
activities.tip_zh: 橡皮筋上的差別很小，所以要仔細聽、多試幾次。如果同伴聽不出來，那也是一個結果。橡皮筋要離臉遠一點。

activities.title_en: Who Is Singing? Same Note, Different Voices
activities.title_zh: 是誰在唱？同一個音，不同的聲音

materials.en: A pitch from this page: play the C4 key in lesson 1 or the whole string
materials.zh: 從本頁取一個音：在第一課彈 C4 鍵或整根弦

materials.en: Four or five volunteers, or a recorder or ukulele if you have them
materials.zh: 四、五位自願的同學；有直笛或烏克麗麗也可以

materials.en: Paper and pencil for each listener
materials.zh: 每位聽的同學一張紙和一支筆

steps.en: Everyone listens to the pitch from the page. Each volunteer, one at a time, sings or plays that same pitch for two seconds, behind the others.
steps.zh: 大家先聽頁面上的音。每位自願的同學一次一位，站在大家後面，把同一個音唱或吹兩秒。

steps.en: Listeners keep their eyes closed and write down who it was, and one word for the sound.
steps.zh: 聽的人閉著眼睛，寫下是誰，再寫一個形容聲音的詞。

steps.en: Now start the note in two ways: very gently, and with a sharp “t” or “d” at the front. Does that change how easy it is to know the sound?
steps.zh: 再用兩種方式開始這個音：很輕柔地開始，和在前面加一個清脆的「ㄊ」或「ㄉ」。這樣有沒有改變辨認的難易？

steps.en: Talk about it: pitch was the same, so what told you apart?
steps.zh: 討論：音高是一樣的，那是什麼讓你分辨出來的？

activities.tip_en: Each person's voice has its own timbre, just as every instrument does. This is a good chance to practice words for sound in English: bright, dark, warm, soft, sharp, round.
activities.tip_zh: 每個人的聲音都有自己的音色，就像每一種樂器一樣。這也是練習用英文形容聲音的好機會：bright、dark、warm、soft、sharp、round。

links_head.en: Before, around, and after this lesson
links_head.zh: 這一課的前面、旁邊和後面

links.en: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
links.zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
links.note_en: Half a string shakes twice as fast. This lesson showed that a whole string also shakes in halves, at the same time.
links.note_zh: 弦長一半，振動快一倍。這一課看到整根弦同時也在一半一半地振動。

links.en: How Does Sound Reach Your Ears?
links.note_en: Sound is a vibration that travels through the air. That lesson follows it to your ear.
links.note_zh: 聲音是在空氣中傳遞的振動。那一課一路講到你的耳朵。

links.en: What Is a Beat?
links.note_en: Pitch and tone color are about one note. This lesson is about time: the steady beat under the music.
links.note_zh: 音高和音色說的是一個音。下一課講時間：音樂底下穩定的拍子。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The frequencies and wave shapes are computed by the page itself and covered by automatic tests.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；頻率與波形由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試。

sources.en: Timbre: the ANSI definition, the role of the spectrum and the time envelope (attack, decay, sustain, release), and the effect of removing the attack
sources.zh: 音色：ANSI 的定義、頻譜與時間包絡（起音、衰減、維持、釋放）的角色，以及去掉起音的效果

sources.en: Harmonic frequencies on a string fixed at both ends are n times the fundamental; nodes and antinodes; the first overtone is the second harmonic
sources.zh: 兩端固定的弦，諧波頻率是基頻的 n 倍；節點與腹點；第一泛音是第二諧波

sources.en: The harmonic series, fundamental, partial, and overtone; the fundamental is generally perceived as the pitch; piano inharmonicity
sources.zh: 泛音列、基音、分音、泛音；基音通常被聽成音高；鋼琴的不諧和性

sources.en: A stiff string's partials are no longer exactly harmonic; strings under low tension, such as bass piano strings, show it most
sources.zh: 有硬度的弦，分音不再剛好是整數倍；低張力的弦（例如鋼琴低音弦）最明顯

sources.en: Helmholtz, On the Sensations of Tone (Ellis translation): a string struck in its middle loses its second partial; the clarinet reinforces the uneven partials; how a bow carries the string
sources.zh: 亥姆霍茲《論音的感覺》（艾利斯英譯）：弦在正中間被敲，第二分音消失；單簧管加強奇數分音；弓怎麼帶著弦走

sources.en: Helmholtz published Sensations of Tone in 1863
sources.zh: 亥姆霍茲在 1863 年出版這本書

sources.en: The clarinet plays approximately the odd members of the series only; the missing even harmonics
sources.zh: 單簧管（大約）只發出泛音列中奇數的那些；偶數諧波缺少

sources.en: Clarinet: a cylindrical stopped pipe in which primarily the odd harmonics are reinforced
sources.zh: 單簧管：近似圓柱閉管，主要加強奇數諧波

sources.en: A string plucked at the center has prominent odd harmonics and weak even ones; plucked near the bridge it has stronger high harmonics
sources.zh: 弦在正中間撥，奇數諧波明顯、偶數諧波弱；靠近琴橋撥，高諧波較強
sources.src: Middle Tennessee State University, W. Roberston, Fourier transforms module

sources.en: Square wave: only odd harmonics (1, 1/3, 1/5…)
Sawtooth wave: all the integer harmonics, with amplitude 1/k
sources.zh: 鋸齒波：所有整數諧波，振幅 1/k

sources.en: Triangle wave: only odd harmonics, falling off as the inverse square of the harmonic number
sources.zh: 三角波：只有奇數諧波，依諧波編號的平方反比變小

sources.en: A piano's strings are struck by felt-covered wooden hammers
sources.zh: 鋼琴的弦由包著毛氈的木槌敲響

sources.en: Stick–slip motion is used to generate musical notes in bowed string instruments
sources.zh: 弓弦樂器靠「黏住、滑開」的運動發出樂音

sources.en: Timbre (音色, 音品): the Ministry of Education Dictionary entries
sources.zh: 音色、音品：教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》詞條
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「音品」

sources.en: Fundamental tone (基音), harmonic and overtone (泛音) in the Ministry of Education Dictionary
sources.zh: 基音、泛音：教育部辭典詞條
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「泛音」

sources.en: Chinese terms: timbre 音色, tone color 音色, overtone 泛音, harmonic 諧波／泛音, fundamental tone 基音, waveform 波形, node 波節, antinode 波腹, attack 起音
sources.zh: 中文名詞：timbre 音色、tone color 音色、overtone 泛音、harmonic 諧波／泛音、fundamental tone 基音、waveform 波形、node 波節、antinode 波腹、attack 起音
sources.src: 國家教育研究院「學術名詞資訊網」

sources.en: The erhu: “beautiful timbre, strong expressiveness… soft and strong”
sources.zh: 二胡：「音色優美、表現力強……音色剛柔多變」
sources.src: 教育百科〈二胡〉（臺灣音樂館傳統民族樂器資料庫）

sources.en: Safe listening: headphone volume to 60% of maximum, personal audio devices less than one hour a day
sources.zh: 安全聆聽：耳機音量不超過最大的 60%、個人音響裝置每天少於一小時

sources.en: Taiwan's 12-year curriculum: arts (music) 音 E-Ⅳ-4

lessons.title: What Is a Beat?
lessons.blurb_en: Start a pendulum metronome, change its speed, and count the strong and weak beats in twos, threes, and fours. Then tap along and see how close you land to the beat.
lessons.blurb_zh: 啟動擺錘節拍器、改變它的速度，數一數二拍、三拍、四拍裡的強拍與弱拍。再跟著敲，看你離拍子有多近。
lessons.big_idea_en: A beat is a steady pulse that cuts time into equal steps. Strong and weak beats come back in a repeating pattern, which groups them into bars of two, three, or four. The speed is counted in beats per minute.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 拍是穩定的脈搏，把時間切成一樣長的格。強拍和弱拍照著一個圖樣一直回來，把拍分成二拍、三拍或四拍的小節。速度則用每分鐘幾拍來數。

lab.how_en: Press Start and watch the rod. Every time it reaches one end, that is one beat, and you hear a click. The row of lights on top shows which beat of the bar you are on. The gold light is the strong beat. Drag the gold weight up for slower and down for faster, or use the slider. Choose two, three, or four beats in a bar and listen for the strong beat that keeps coming back.
lab.how_zh: 按「開始」，看擺桿。每次擺到一端，就是一拍，你會聽到一聲喀。頂上一排燈顯示現在是小節的第幾拍，金色的燈是強拍。把金色重錘往上拖就變慢、往下拖就變快，也可以用滑桿。選每小節二拍、三拍或四拍，聽那個一直回來的強拍。

legend.en: Gold light: the strong beat, the first beat of each bar
legend.zh: 金色燈：強拍，每小節的第一拍

legend.en: Cyan lights: the other beats of the bar
legend.zh: 青色燈：小節裡的其他拍

legend.en: Gold weight: higher is slower, lower is faster (schematic)
legend.zh: 金色重錘：越高越慢、越低越快（示意）

lab.scale_en: The speed range is 40 to 180 beats per minute. At 180, there are three beats every second.
lab.scale_zh: 速度範圍是每分鐘 40 到 180 拍。180 拍時，每秒三拍。
lab.credit_html: The clicks are made by your browser, with a different pitch for strong and weak beats. They are timed on the browser's audio clock, so the sound and the pendulum agree. · 喀喀聲由瀏覽器合成，強拍與弱拍的音高不同；它們用瀏覽器的聲音時鐘排程，所以聲音和擺錘是一致的。

paras: Think of a song you love and tap your foot along with it. Everyone in the room taps at the same speed, and nobody had to count. What you are tapping is the beat. A beat is the basic unit of time in music, the pulse, and it keeps going whether the melody has a long note or a short one.

Beats come one after another, each the same length, like the ticks of a clock. We say how fast the beats are with the word tempo, which is Italian for “time.” Tempo is measured in beats per minute, or BPM. At 60 BPM there is exactly one beat every second, like the second hand of a clock. At 120 BPM the beats are twice as fast. For comparison, the resting pulse of a person aged ten or older is 60 to 100 beats per minute, counted in the same unit.

But beats are not all the same. Some feel stronger and some weaker, and the pattern keeps coming back. A set of beats from one strong beat to the next is called a bar, or a measure. The first beat of the bar is the downbeat, and it is usually the strongest. The pattern of strong and weak beats is the meter.

The most common patterns are twos, threes, and fours. In two beats, the pattern is strong, weak, like a march step. In three beats, it is strong, weak, weak, and you count one-two-three. In four beats, it is strong, weak, medium, weak. Written music shows this with a time signature. In 3/4, the top number says there are three beats in each bar, and the bottom number says that a quarter note gets one beat.

Chinese traditional music has its own names for the same idea. The strongest beat is the 板 (bǎn), struck on a wooden clapper. The weaker beats are the 眼 (yǎn), marked with a drumstick. “One 板 and one 眼” means two beats in a bar, and “one 板 and three 眼” means four. In nanguan music, the beats are counted in 撩拍, with its own clapper called the 拍板.

A metronome keeps the beat for you. The mechanical kind has a rod that swings like a pendulum and a weight that slides up the rod to make it slower. A German inventor named Johann Maelzel patented one in 1815, after an earlier design by Dietrich Winkel. Beethoven was soon the first notable composer to write metronome numbers in his music. Even so, the old Italian words such as allegro and andante are only rough guides, and different books give them different numbers.
paras_zh: 想一首你喜歡的歌，跟著它用腳打拍子。房間裡每個人敲的速度都一樣，而且沒有人需要數。你敲的就是拍。拍是音樂裡最基本的時間單位，是脈搏；不管旋律是長音還是短音，它都一直走下去。
拍一個接著一個，每一拍一樣長，像時鐘的滴答。我們用「速度」（tempo，義大利文是「時間」的意思）來說拍有多快，單位是每分鐘幾拍，簡稱 BPM。60 BPM 就是每秒剛好一拍，像時鐘的秒針；120 BPM 就快一倍。作為對照，十歲以上的人靜止時的脈搏是每分鐘 60 到 100 下，用的是同一種單位。
可是拍不全是一樣的。有些感覺比較強、有些比較弱，而且這個圖樣一直回來。從一個強拍到下一個強拍之間的拍，合成一組，叫做一個小節（measure，也叫 bar）。小節的第一拍是強拍（downbeat），通常最強。強弱拍的圖樣叫做拍子（meter）。
最常見的圖樣是二拍、三拍和四拍。二拍子是強、弱，像行進的腳步；三拍子是強、弱、弱，數成一二三；四拍子是強、弱、次強、弱。樂譜用「拍子記號」（拍號）把它寫下來。在 3/4 裡，上面的數字說每小節有三拍，下面的數字說以四分音符為一拍。
中國傳統音樂對同一件事有自己的名字。最強的拍叫「板」，用拍板敲出來；比較弱的拍叫「眼」，用鼓簽標出來。「一板一眼」是一小節兩拍，「一板三眼」是一小節四拍。南管音樂則用「撩拍」來數拍，並且有自己叫做「拍板」的樂器。

節拍器可以替你保持拍子。機械式的節拍器有一根像鐘擺一樣擺動的桿子，和一個沿著桿子往上滑就會變慢的重錘。德國發明家約翰・梅爾策爾（Johann Maelzel）在 1815 年取得專利，在這之前已有迪特里希・溫克爾（Dietrich Winkel）的設計。貝多芬很快就成為第一位把節拍器數字寫進樂譜的知名作曲家。即使如此，allegro、andante 這些舊的義大利文，也只是大略的指引，不同的書給它們的數字也不一樣。
questions: A song is played at 120 BPM. How long is one beat, and how many beats are there in 10 seconds?
What does the time signature 3/4 tell you?
A friend says, “Tempo and beat are the same thing.” How would you explain the difference?
answers: One beat lasts 60 ÷ 120 = 0.5 seconds. In 10 seconds there are 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 beats.
The top number, 3, means there are three beats in each bar. The bottom number, 4, means that a quarter note gets one beat. The pattern is usually strong, weak, weak.
The beat is the steady pulse itself, one step of equal length after another. Tempo is how fast those beats go, usually counted in beats per minute.

vocab.ex: Clap on every beat of the song.
vocab.exzh: 跟著這首歌的每一拍拍手。

vocab.ex: Put two fingers on your wrist to feel your pulse.
vocab.exzh: 把兩根手指放在手腕上，感覺你的脈搏。

vocab.ex: The band played the song at a fast tempo.
vocab.exzh: 樂團用很快的速度演奏這首歌。

vocab.ex: Each measure of this song has four beats.
vocab.exzh: 這首歌的每一個小節有四拍。

vocab.ex: A waltz has a meter of three beats.
vocab.exzh: 圓舞曲的拍子是三拍。

vocab.ex: Put an accent on the first beat of the bar.
vocab.exzh: 在小節的第一拍加重音。

vocab.ex: She practices the piano with a metronome.
vocab.exzh: 她用節拍器練鋼琴。

vocab.ex: A drummer must keep a steady beat.
vocab.exzh: 鼓手必須維持穩定的拍子。

The song is four minutes long

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: One beat every 1.2 seconds. Watch where the weight sits: high on the rod.
parts.text_zh: 每 1.2 秒一拍。看看重錘在哪裡：在桿子的高處。

parts.text_en: Nearly three beats every second. The weight slides down the rod.
parts.text_zh: 每秒將近三拍。重錘滑到桿子的低處。

parts.text_en: Count one-two-three, one-two-three. The gold light comes back every third beat.
parts.text_zh: 數一二三、一二三。金色的燈每三拍回來一次。

parts.text_en: Compare the clicks with a clock that has a second hand. They match.
parts.text_zh: 拿喀喀聲和有秒針的時鐘比一比，它們是一致的。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then switch between two, three, and four beats and listen. How do you know which one you are hearing?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後在二拍、三拍、四拍之間切換並仔細聽。你怎麼知道自己聽到的是哪一種？

tap.lead_en: Choose a speed and press Start. You will hear four count-in beats, and then you tap the drum sixteen times along with the clicks. You can tap with a mouse, a finger, or the space bar. The graph shows each tap: a dot above the middle line is late, and a dot below is early. Green dots are within 50 milliseconds, which is one twentieth of a second.
tap.lead_zh: 選一個速度、按「開始」。你會先聽到四拍預備，然後跟著喀喀聲在鼓面上敲十六下。可以用滑鼠、手指或空白鍵。圖上畫出每一下：在中線上方的點是晚了，在下方的點是早了。綠色的點在 50 毫秒以內，也就是二十分之一秒。

meterq.en: How Many Beats in a Bar?
meterq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays three bars. Listen for the strong beat that keeps coming back and count the beats from one strong beat to the next. Then choose two, three, or four.
meterq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題播三個小節。聽那個一直回來的強拍，數從一個強拍到下一個強拍有幾拍，再選二、三或四。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: Unlike pitch and tone color, beat, speed, and time signatures are named directly in the elementary arts curriculum for music.
curric.lead_zh: 和音高、音色不一樣，拍、速度和拍號都直接寫在國小藝術領域音樂的課綱裡。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Beat · 拍子背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A clapper, a pendulum, Beethoven’s numbers, and some Italian words
culture_cards.title_zh: 一塊拍板、一個擺錘、貝多芬的數字，和幾個義大利字
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people keep and name the beat.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼守住拍子、又怎麼為它命名的四個小故事。

cards.en: 板 and 眼 in Chinese music
cards.body_en: In traditional Chinese opera and music, the strongest beat of a bar is the 板, struck with a wooden clapper. The weaker beats are the 眼, marked with a drumstick. So “one 板 and three 眼” is a bar of four beats. The phrase also became an everyday saying for someone who does things by the book. In nanguan music, the beat is called 撩拍 instead, kept with a clapper made of several wooden pieces.
cards.body_zh: 在中國傳統戲曲與音樂裡，小節裡最強的拍叫「板」，用拍板敲出來；比較弱的拍叫「眼」，用鼓簽標出來。所以「一板三眼」就是一小節四拍。這句話後來也變成一句日常的俗語，形容人做事一絲不苟。南管音樂則改稱「撩拍」，用好幾片木板做成的拍板來打拍子。

cards.body_en: A mechanical metronome uses an upside-down pendulum: a rod with a fixed weight at the bottom and a weight you can slide. Slide it up and the rod swings slower. Slide it down and it swings faster. Most are adjustable from about 40 to 208 beats per minute. Dietrich Winkel built a version in Amsterdam in 1814, and Johann Maelzel added a numbered scale and patented it in 1815.
cards.body_zh: 機械節拍器用的是倒過來的擺：一根桿子，下面有固定的重錘，另外還有一個可以滑動的重錘。往上滑，擺得比較慢；往下滑，擺得比較快。大多數可以調到大約每分鐘 40 到 208 拍。迪特里希・溫克爾 1814 年在阿姆斯特丹做出一種版本，約翰・梅爾策爾加上有數字的刻度，並在 1815 年申請專利。

cards.body_en: Maelzel knew Beethoven, and Beethoven became the first notable composer to write specific metronome marks in his music. This was in December 1815, in the corrected score of his Cantata op. 112. Since then, a mark such as M.M. = 60, for Maelzel’s Metronome, has told a player exactly how fast to go: sixty beats per minute.
cards.body_zh: 梅爾策爾認識貝多芬，而貝多芬成為第一位把明確的節拍器數字寫進樂譜的知名作曲家。那是 1815 年 12 月，在他的清唱劇作品 112 的修正稿上。從那時起，像 M.M. = 60（M.M. 是梅爾策爾節拍器的縮寫）這樣的標記，就明確告訴演奏者要多快：每分鐘六十拍。

cards.body_en: Tempo is the Italian word for “time.” Well-known Italian speed words include allegro, which means “cheerful,” andante, “walking pace,” and presto, “quickly.” People often give each word a range of BPM numbers, but the books do not agree, and one reference calls the numbers “very rough approximations.” The speed words tell you a feeling and a rough speed, and a metronome mark tells you the exact one.
cards.body_zh: Tempo 是義大利文的「時間」。有名的義大利文速度詞包括 allegro（輕快、愉快）、andante（走路的速度）和 presto（很快）。人們常給每個詞一個 BPM 的範圍，但不同的書意見不一，有一份參考資料還說這些數字只是「非常粗略的近似」。速度詞告訴你一種感覺和大略的快慢，節拍器的標記才告訴你精確的數字。

myths.myth_en: Beat and rhythm are exactly the same thing.
myths.myth_zh: 拍和節奏是完全一樣的東西。
myths.fact_en: The beat is the steady pulse that you would tap your foot to. Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds that moves over it, and it can be much more complicated than the beat.
myths.fact_zh: 拍是你會用腳去打的穩定脈搏；節奏是在它上面進行的長短聲音的圖樣，可以比拍複雜得多。

myths.myth_en: All beats have the same strength.
myths.myth_zh: 每一拍的力度都一樣。
myths.fact_en: In most music some beats are stressed and some are unstressed. The pattern of strong and weak beats coming back again and again is what we call meter.
myths.fact_zh: 大多數音樂裡，有些拍是重的、有些是輕的。強弱拍一再回來的圖樣，就叫拍子（meter）。

myths.myth_en: A faster song has more beats in each bar.
myths.myth_zh: 越快的歌，每小節的拍數越多。
myths.fact_en: The number of beats in a bar and the speed are two different things. A song in three beats can be slow or fast. The top number of the time signature counts beats in a bar. The BPM counts beats in a minute.
myths.fact_zh: 每小節幾拍和速度是兩件事。三拍子的歌可以慢也可以快。拍號上面的數字數的是每小節的拍數，BPM 數的是每分鐘的拍數。

myths.myth_en: “Allegro” means exactly 120 BPM.
myths.myth_zh: 「Allegro」就是剛好每分鐘 120 拍。
myths.fact_en: The speed words are rough guides. Two common references give different ranges for allegro, and even the order of two of the words, largo and adagio, is the opposite of what it was in the Baroque period. Only a metronome mark gives an exact number.
myths.fact_zh: 速度詞只是大略的指引。兩份常見的參考資料給 allegro 的範圍就不一樣，連 largo 和 adagio 兩個詞誰快誰慢，現在也和巴洛克時期相反。只有節拍器標記才給精確的數字。

tricks.body_en: Every beat is the same length.
tricks.body_zh: 每一拍一樣長。

tricks.body_en: Double the BPM, and the beats are twice as fast.
tricks.body_zh: BPM 加倍，拍子就快一倍。

tricks.title_en: Count to the next strong beat
tricks.body_en: The beats from one strong beat to the next make a bar.
tricks.body_zh: 從一個強拍到下一個強拍之間的拍，是一個小節。

tricks.body_en: In 3/4, the top number says three beats, the bottom number says quarter notes.
tricks.body_zh: 3/4 裡，上面說三拍，下面說以四分音符為一拍。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 開始之前

safety.en: The lights and dots flash with the beat, up to three times a second at 180 BPM. For some people with photosensitive epilepsy, lights flashing at about three to sixty times a second can trigger a seizure. If you or anyone in your class is sensitive, switch the flashing off with the switch under the model. The sound and the pendulum still work.
safety.zh: 燈和圓點會跟著拍子閃，180 BPM 時每秒最多三次。對患有光敏感性癲癇的人來說，大約每秒三次到六十次的閃光可能引發發作。如果你或班上有人是敏感的，請用模型下方的開關把閃爍關掉；聲音和擺錘仍然會動。

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: When you tap or clap in class, use your hands or a soft pad. Do not hit a phone screen or a desk hard, and do not clap close to anyone’s ears.
safety.zh: 在課堂上敲或拍手時，用手或軟墊就好。不要用力敲手機螢幕或桌子，也不要在別人耳朵旁邊拍手。

materials.en: A clock or timer with seconds
materials.zh: 有秒針或秒數的時鐘或計時器

materials.en: Paper and pencil
This page, for the metronome

steps.en: Sit quietly for a minute. Put two fingers on the inside of your wrist, gently, and find your pulse.
steps.zh: 安靜坐一分鐘。把兩根手指輕輕放在手腕內側，找到你的脈搏。

steps.en: Count the beats for 15 seconds and multiply by four. That is your pulse in beats per minute.
steps.zh: 數 15 秒的下數，乘以四，就是你每分鐘的脈搏數。

steps.en: Set the metronome to a number close to yours. Listen: is your pulse faster or slower than the clicks?
steps.zh: 把節拍器調到接近你的數字。聽聽看：你的脈搏比喀喀聲快還是慢？

steps.en: Jump up and down for 30 seconds and count again. What changed? Compare your numbers with the 60 to 100 that is normal at rest.
steps.zh: 原地跳 30 秒，再數一次。有什麼改變？把你的數字和靜止時正常的 60 到 100 比一比。

activities.tip_en: This is not a medical test. Everyone's pulse is a little different. Do not press hard on your neck. Use your wrist.
activities.tip_zh: 這不是醫療檢查，每個人的脈搏都有一點不一樣。不要用力壓脖子，用手腕就好。

activities.title_en: Human Metronome: 板 and 眼

materials.en: A desk or a pair of wooden blocks for the strong beat
materials.zh: 一張桌子或一對木塊，當作強拍

materials.en: Your hands, for the weak beats
The metronome on this page

steps.en: Set the metronome to 80 BPM and four beats in a bar. Listen to the high click, the strong beat.
steps.zh: 把節拍器調到 80 BPM、每小節四拍。聽那個比較高的喀，就是強拍。

steps.en: Strike the desk on the strong beat, the 板, and tap your knee on every other beat, the 眼. That is “one 板 and three 眼.”
steps.zh: 在強拍（板）敲桌子，其他每一拍在膝蓋上輕拍（眼）。這就是「一板三眼」。

steps.en: Switch to two beats in a bar: “one 板 and one 眼.” Then to three beats. Which one feels like a march? Which one feels like a waltz?
steps.zh: 換成每小節兩拍：「一板一眼」。再換成三拍。哪一種像行進？哪一種像圓舞曲？

steps.en: Take turns being the metronome for the class: one student keeps the 板, and the class keeps the 眼.
steps.zh: 輪流當全班的節拍器：一位同學打「板」，全班打「眼」。

activities.tip_en: Keep the volume of the metronome low, and use the soft part of your hand. Tapping softly lets everyone hear the clicks.
activities.tip_zh: 節拍器音量調小，用手掌軟的部分輕拍，這樣大家才聽得到喀喀聲。

sources.zh: 拍子：強弱拍規律地一再出現的圖樣

sources.zh: 小節（bar 或 measure）是用直線隔出來的一段音樂

sources.en: 拍 and 拍子: units that count musical rhythm (二拍子, 三拍子, 四拍子)
sources.zh: 拍、拍子：計算音樂節奏的單位（二拍子、三拍子、四拍子）

sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「小節」

sources.zh: 拍子記號（拍號）：上面是每小節拍數、下面是拍子的基本單位；3/4 表示以四分音符為一拍、每小節三拍

sources.en: 板眼: the strong beat struck on the clapper is the 板; the secondary and weak beats marked with the drumstick are the 眼
sources.zh: 板眼：以鼓板敲擊的強拍為「板」；以簽敲鼓按拍的次強拍和弱拍為「眼」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「板眼」

sources.en: 一板三眼: four beats in a bar; 一板一眼: two beats in a bar
sources.zh: 一板三眼：一小節四拍；一板一眼：一小節兩拍

sources.zh: 脈搏：十歲以上兒童與成人靜止時每分鐘 60 到 100 下

lessons.title: How Do You Tell a Musician “Louder” or “Faster”?
lessons.title_zh: 怎麼告訴演奏的人「大聲一點」「快一點」？
lessons.blurb_en: Play one short melody with a loudness sign and a speed word, from pianissimo to fortissimo and from largo to presto, and watch the notes get brighter and thicker as the music gets louder.
lessons.blurb_zh: 同一段短旋律，配上一個力度記號和一個速度詞，從 pianissimo 到 fortissimo、從 largo 到 presto，看音符隨著越來越大聲而變亮、變粗。
lessons.big_idea_en: Notes tell a player what to play. Italian signs tell the player how loud and how fast. Dynamics say how loud, and tempo says how fast, and the two can be changed on their own.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 音符告訴演奏的人要彈什麼；義大利文的記號告訴他要多大聲、多快。力度說多大聲，速度說多快，兩者可以各自改變。

lab.how_en: Below is a short melody, written for this page, drawn as bars. Choose a loudness, a speed, and a shape, and press play. The notes and the rhythm never change. Only the signs change. Brighter, thicker bars are louder. Try a crescendo (<) and a diminuendo (>) too.
lab.how_zh: 下面是為這一頁寫的一段短旋律，畫成長條。選一個力度、一個速度、一個形狀，再按播放。音和節奏從來沒有變，變的只有記號。越亮越粗的長條越大聲。也試試漸強（<）和漸弱（>）。

paras: Imagine you are a composer, and the musician who will play your piece is far away, or lives a hundred years after you. You can write the notes. But how loud should they be? How fast? Notes alone only tell the player which pitch and how long. To say the rest, composers add signs and words.

There are two questions. How loud is the music? That is called dynamics. How fast is it? That is called tempo. For loudness, composers use letters. The letter p stands for piano, which means “soft.” The letter f stands for forte, which means “loud.” The word mezzo means “half,” so mp is a medium soft and mf is a medium loud. Doubling a letter makes it stronger: pp is pianissimo, very soft, and ff is fortissimo, very loud.

These signs are always relative. A p never means a precise amount of loudness. It only says that this part should be quieter than the parts marked f. In fact, a tuba playing mezzo piano can be louder than a guitar playing forte. Each player decides what soft and loud are for the instrument and the room.

Loudness can also change gradually. Crescendo means “growing,” and it is drawn as two lines that open to the right, like <. Diminuendo means “dwindling,” and it is drawn as two lines that close to the right, like >. These signs are sometimes called hairpins. In Chinese they are 漸強 and 漸弱.

For speed, the words are also Italian. From slow to fast, a few well-known ones are largo (“broad”), adagio (“at ease”), andante (“walking”), moderato (“moderate”), allegro (“lively”), and presto (“quick”). To change the speed, ritardando means slowing down, and accelerando means speeding up. Such words give a feeling and a rough speed. A metronome mark, which you met in the last lesson, gives the exact number.

Why Italian? The practice grew up in the 17th and 18th centuries, when most composers were Italian. Later, composers also wrote in French, German, and English. And why is a piano called a piano? It is short for pianoforte, “soft and loud.” Early in the 1700s, the keyboard instrument made by Cristofori could play both, depending on how hard the player pressed the key. The harpsichord and the organ could not do this.
paras_zh: 想像你是一位作曲家，要演奏你作品的人在很遠的地方，或是在你之後一百年才出生。你可以把音寫下來，可是要多大聲？多快？光靠音符，只能告訴演奏的人音高和長短。要說明其餘的事，作曲家就加上記號和字。
有兩個問題。音樂有多大聲？這叫做「力度」（dynamics）。音樂有多快？這叫做「速度」（tempo）。說明大聲小聲，作曲家用字母：p 是 piano，意思是「弱」；f 是 forte，意思是「強」。mezzo 是「一半」，所以 mp 是中弱、mf 是中強。字母重疊就更強：pp 是 pianissimo，很弱；ff 是 fortissimo，很強。
這些記號永遠是相對的。p 絕對不是指一個精確的音量，它只是說這一段應該比標 f 的段落安靜。事實上，大號吹 mezzo piano，可能比吉他彈 forte 還大聲。什麼叫弱、什麼叫強，要由演奏者依樂器和場地來決定。
大聲小聲也可以慢慢改變。crescendo 是「增長」，畫成向右打開的兩條線，像 <；diminuendo 是「逐漸減少」，畫成向右合起來的兩條線，像 >。這兩個記號有時被叫做「髮夾」。中文是「漸強」和「漸弱」。
速度的詞也是義大利文。由慢到快，幾個有名的是 largo（寬廣）、adagio（從容）、andante（走路的速度）、moderato（中等）、allegro（輕快）和 presto（很快）。要改變速度，ritardando 是漸慢、accelerando 是漸快。這些詞給的是一種感覺和大略的速度；你在上一課認識的節拍器標記，才給精確的數字。
為什麼是義大利文？這個做法是在十七、十八世紀發展起來的，當時大多數的作曲家是義大利人。後來作曲家也用法文、德文和英文。那鋼琴為什麼叫 piano？它是 pianoforte 的縮寫，意思是「弱與強」。十八世紀初，克里斯托弗里（Cristofori）做出的這種鍵盤樂器，可以依彈奏的人按鍵多用力，彈出弱和強。大鍵琴和管風琴就做不到。
questions: What is the difference between dynamics and tempo?
Why can't a sign such as f be given one fixed loudness number?
A player sees mf, then a < sign, then f. What happens to the music?
answers: Dynamics are about how loud the music is. Tempo is about how fast it is. They are separate, so a melody can be soft and fast, or loud and slow.
Dynamic signs are relative. They only say how one part compares with another. The same sign can mean a different volume in different pieces, on different instruments, and in different rooms.
The music starts moderately loud, then gets gradually louder, until it reaches loud. The notes and the speed stay the same.

vocab.ex: The dynamics of this song go from very soft to very loud.
vocab.exzh: 這首歌的力度從很弱到很強。

vocab.ex: The score has a marking at the top that says allegro.
vocab.exzh: 樂譜上方有一個寫著 allegro 的記號。

vocab.ex: The music gradually gets louder.
vocab.exzh: 音樂逐漸變大聲。

vocab.ex: The drums play a long crescendo at the end.
vocab.exzh: 鼓在結尾奏出一段很長的漸強。

vocab.ex: The last bars have a diminuendo to silence.
vocab.exzh: 最後幾個小節漸弱到安靜。

vocab.ex: Soft and loud are relative: they depend on what you compare with.
vocab.exzh: 弱和強是相對的：要看你拿什麼來比。

vocab.ex: Please turn down the volume a little.
vocab.exzh: 請把音量調小一點。

vocab.ex: Allegro is a lively speed.
vocab.exzh: Allegro 是一種輕快的速度。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_en: The bars are dim and thin
parts.text_en: Same melody, same speed. Only the sign is p. Watch how thin the bars are.
parts.text_zh: 同樣的旋律、同樣的速度，只有記號是 p。看看長條多細。

parts.meta_en: The bars are bright and thick
parts.text_en: Now the sign is f. The notes are the same, and everything else is the same too.
parts.text_zh: 現在記號是 f。音一樣，其他的也都一樣。

parts.text_en: The bars grow brighter and thicker from the first note to the last.
parts.text_zh: 長條從第一個音到最後一個音，越來越亮、越來越粗。

parts.text_en: The melody plays twice. Listen for how long it takes each time.
parts.text_zh: 旋律播兩次。聽聽每一次花多久。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then combine them: a soft, fast melody, or a loud, slow one. Dynamics and tempo are separate dials.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後把它們組合起來：又弱又快的旋律，或又強又慢的旋律。力度和速度是兩個各自獨立的旋鈕。

signq.lead_en: Six questions. First you hear one reference note at a medium loudness, and then the melody. Is the melody softer, louder, getting louder, or getting softer? Choose the matching word.
signq.lead_zh: 六道題。你會先聽到一個中等音量的參考音，再聽旋律。旋律是比較小聲、比較大聲、越來越大聲，還是越來越小聲？選出對得上的詞。

tempoq.lead_en: Five questions. The same four notes are played twice, at two different speeds. The question names one of the two speed words. Pick the version that has that speed. The speed ladder shows the order from slow to fast.
tempoq.lead_zh: 五道題。同樣四個音用兩種速度各播一次。題目會說出其中一個速度詞，選出符合那個速度的版本。速度階梯顯示由慢到快的順序。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The elementary arts curriculum names dynamics and speed directly. It does not list crescendo or diminuendo by name. Those two come from the music itself.
curric.lead_zh: 國小藝術領域的課綱直接寫到力度和速度，但沒有點名「漸強」「漸弱」；那兩個詞是從音樂本身來的。

items.note_en: Music terms are listed together with music symbols and reading music.

items.area: 自然科學領域・學習內容說明
items.text: 可藉由手的觸摸、觀察鼓面豆子的跳動、弦的振動等活動，察覺物體振動會產生聲音，而振動的強弱會影響音量的大小。
items.note_en: A stronger vibration gives a louder sound. This is the physics under the word “forte.”
items.note_zh: 振動越強，聲音越大。這就是「forte」這個詞底下的物理。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Signs · 記號背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A name, a language, a tuba, and two words that swapped
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個名字、一種語言、一支大號，和兩個對調的詞
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about the words musicians use for loud, soft, and fast.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於音樂家用來說大聲、小聲、快的那些詞的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: The piano takes its name from the Italian words for soft and loud. An inventory kept by the Medici family of Florence shows that Bartolomeo Cristofori had a piano by 1700. Cristofori called it a keyboard “of piano and forte.” Unlike the harpsichord, it changed its volume with the touch of the player, and the harder you press the key, the louder the sound.
cards.body_zh: 鋼琴（piano）的名字來自義大利文的「弱」和「強」。佛羅倫斯的梅迪奇家族的財物清冊顯示，克里斯托弗里（Bartolomeo Cristofori）在 1700 年已經有一架鋼琴。他把它叫做「有弱有強的」鍵盤樂器。它和大鍵琴不一樣，音量會隨彈奏的人的觸鍵而變，鍵按得越用力，聲音就越大。

cards.body_en: Italian is typically used because it was the language of most composers when these words became common. The practice developed in the 17th and 18th centuries. Later, composers wrote speed words in their own languages too. Beethoven was one of the first German composers to do so, but only a little. Later still, Schumann and Mahler wrote more and more of their instructions in German.
cards.body_zh: 會用義大利文，是因為這些詞開始普遍的時候，大多數作曲家說的就是義大利文。這個做法在十七、十八世紀發展起來。後來作曲家也用自己的語言寫速度詞。貝多芬是最早用德文的德國作曲家之一，但用得很少。後來舒曼和馬勒，更是把越來越多的指示寫成德文。

cards.en: Soft and loud depend on the instrument
cards.body_en: Dynamic markings are always relative. Because of that, a tuba playing mezzo piano will likely be louder than a guitar playing forte. A high instrument such as the piccolo can sound loud even when it is not very strong. This is why a conductor listens to the whole group before deciding what “soft” means.
cards.body_zh: 力度記號永遠是相對的。所以大號吹 mezzo piano，很可能比吉他彈 forte 還大聲。像短笛這種高音樂器，就算不是真的很用力，也可能聽起來很響。這就是為什麼指揮要先聽整個團，才決定「弱」是什麼意思。

cards.zh: largo 和 adagio 對調的時候
cards.body_en: Words for speed can change their meaning. A modern largo is slower than an adagio. In the Baroque period it was the other way around, and largo was the faster one. Allegretto changed too. This is one more reason why a metronome number is the only exact answer, and why the speed words give only a feeling.
cards.body_zh: 速度的詞，意思也會改變。現代的 largo 比 adagio 慢，但在巴洛克時期剛好相反，largo 比較快。allegretto 的意思也變過。這就是為什麼只有節拍器的數字才是精確的答案，而速度詞只給一種感覺。

myths.myth_en: Forte means a fixed number of decibels.
myths.myth_zh: Forte 就是固定幾分貝。
myths.fact_en: Dynamic markings are always relative. A forte never means a precise level of loudness. It only says to play louder than the soft parts of the same piece.
myths.fact_zh: 力度記號永遠是相對的。forte 不是精確的音量，只是說要比同一首曲子裡弱的部分大聲。

myths.myth_en: Playing louder also means playing faster.
myths.myth_zh: 越大聲，就是越快。
myths.fact_en: Loudness and speed are separate. Dynamics change how loud, and tempo changes how fast. A melody can be quiet and quick, or loud and slow. Special words, ritardando and accelerando, change the speed.
myths.fact_zh: 音量和速度是分開的。力度改變多大聲，速度改變多快。旋律可以又小聲又快，也可以又大聲又慢。改變速度要用另外的詞：ritardando 和 accelerando。

myths.myth_en: Allegro means an exact number of beats per minute.
myths.myth_zh: Allegro 就是精確的每分鐘幾拍。
myths.fact_en: The numbers for the speed words are only very rough approximations, and different books give different ranges. A metronome mark is the only way to write an exact number.
myths.fact_zh: 速度詞的數字只是非常粗略的近似，不同的書給的範圍也不同。只有節拍器標記，才能寫出精確的數字。

myths.myth_en: A louder note is just the same note with the volume knob turned up.
myths.myth_zh: 大聲的音，只是把同一個音的音量鈕轉大。
myths.fact_en: On an acoustic instrument the player changes the sound. On a piano, the harder you press a key, the harder the hammer hits the string and the louder the sound. The note’s character changes a little, too.
myths.fact_zh: 在傳統樂器上，是演奏的人改變聲音。鋼琴上，鍵按得越用力，槌子打弦越用力，聲音就越大；音的性格也會稍微改變。

tricks_head.en: Loud, soft, and fast in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住力度與速度

tricks.title_en: p is soft, f is loud, m is half
tricks.title_zh: p 弱、f 強、m 一半
tricks.body_en: mp is medium soft, and mf is medium loud.
tricks.body_zh: mp 是中弱，mf 是中強。

tricks.body_en: Crescendo opens to the right, and diminuendo closes.
tricks.body_zh: 漸強向右打開，漸弱向右合起來。

tricks.title_en: Dynamics: how loud. Tempo: how fast.
tricks.body_en: They are two separate dials.
tricks.body_zh: 它們是兩個各自獨立的旋鈕。

tricks.title_en: Words give a feeling; the metronome gives a number
tricks.title_zh: 詞給感覺，節拍器給數字
tricks.body_en: Allegro is lively. M.M. = 120 is exact.
tricks.body_zh: Allegro 是輕快；M.M. = 120 才是精確。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。

safety.en: The loudest sign here, fortissimo, is never louder than the loudest sound on the other pages. But if you turn the volume up to hear a soft sign, then a loud sign will be much louder. Move to a quieter room instead of turning the volume up.
safety.zh: 這裡最強的記號 fortissimo，也不會比其他頁面最大的聲音更大。但如果你為了聽清楚弱的記號而把音量調大，強的記號就會大聲很多。請改到比較安靜的地方，不要一直調大音量。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: In the classroom, a crescendo with voices or clapping should stay in a comfortable range. Never clap or shout close to anyone's ears.
safety.zh: 在課堂上，用聲音或拍手做漸強時，要維持在舒服的範圍。千萬不要在別人耳朵旁邊拍手或大叫。

materials.en: The whole class, in a circle or in rows
materials.zh: 全班，圍成圓圈或排成幾列

materials.en: One student as the conductor
Cards with p, mf, f, <, and > written on them

steps.en: Everyone claps lightly together on a steady beat. The conductor shows the card p, then mf, then f. The class matches it.
steps.zh: 大家跟著穩定的拍子輕輕一起拍手。指揮依序出示 p、mf、f 的卡片，全班跟著調整。

steps.en: Now the conductor shows < and slowly raises the hands. The class gets louder, little by little, and stops before it is too loud.
steps.zh: 接著指揮出示 <，慢慢舉高雙手。全班一點一點變大聲，在太大聲之前停下來。

steps.en: Try > the same way, and then try a crescendo that ends in silence.
steps.zh: 用同樣的方式試試 >，再試一個結束在安靜裡的漸強。

steps.en: Next, keep the loudness and change only the speed: slower, then faster. Which dial did you turn?
steps.zh: 再來，保持音量、只改變速度：先慢、再快。你轉的是哪一個旋鈕？

activities.tip_en: Clap with soft hands, not hard hands. The loudest sound should still be comfortable, and the conductor decides when to stop.
activities.tip_zh: 用軟軟的手拍，不要用力拍。最大聲也要覺得舒服，由指揮決定什麼時候停。

materials.en: A short sentence, for example: “I did not say that.”
materials.zh: 一句短句，例如：「我沒有那樣說。」

materials.en: Paper and pencil

steps.en: Say the sentence softly, as if it is a secret. Say it loudly, as if you are far away. Write p or f above it.
steps.zh: 用很小聲、像祕密一樣說這句話。再用很大聲、像在很遠的地方一樣說。在句子上面寫 p 或 f。

steps.en: Say it so that it gets louder word by word, and draw a < under it. Then say it getting softer, and draw a >.
steps.zh: 說的時候一個字比一個字大聲，在底下畫 <。再說成越來越小聲，畫 >。

steps.en: Say it slowly and then fast. Which words did you pick for speed, adagio or allegro?
steps.zh: 慢慢說、再快快說。你為速度選了哪個詞，adagio 還是 allegro？

steps.en: Swap sentences with a partner. Read the signs and perform it exactly as written.
steps.zh: 和同伴交換句子。照著記號，把它一模一樣地唸出來。

activities.tip_en: You just did what a composer does: you wrote down how to say something, and someone else can perform it. Use a comfortable speaking volume and keep your voice from straining.
activities.tip_zh: 你剛剛做的就是作曲家做的事：把「怎麼說」寫下來，讓別人也能照著表演。用舒服的說話音量，不要喊到喉嚨用力。

links_head.en: Before, around, and after this lesson
links_head.zh: 這一課的前面、旁邊和後面

links.en: What Is a Beat?
links.note_en: Tempo is how fast the beats go. The metronome number is the exact way to say it.
links.note_zh: 速度就是拍走多快。節拍器的數字是精確的說法。

links.en: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
links.zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
links.note_en: Loudness and pitch are two different things. A note can be high and soft, or low and loud.
links.note_zh: 音量和音高是兩回事。一個音可以又高又弱，也可以又低又強。

links.en: How Does Sound Reach Your Ears?
links.note_en: A bigger vibration makes a louder sound. That lesson follows the sound to your ear.
links.note_zh: 振動越大，聲音越大。那一課一路講到你的耳朵。

links.en: How Do You Read Music?
links.note_en: The next unit puts the notes themselves on paper: the staff, and what each position means.
links.note_zh: 下一個單元要把音本身寫在紙上：五線譜，以及每個位置的意思。
