units.blurb_en: How a tune becomes marks on paper: the staff, note lengths, scales, and why some notes sound good together.
units.blurb_zh: 一段旋律怎麼變成紙上的記號：五線譜、音符的長短、音階，以及為什麼有些音放在一起很好聽。

lessons.title: How Do You Read Music?
lessons.blurb_en: Tap a line or a space on a five-line staff and hear the note, see its name, and see the same note light up on a keyboard. Then find out why a clef changes everything.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在五線譜的一條線或一個間上點一下，聽到那個音、看到它的名字，也看到它在鍵盤上的位置。再看看為什麼譜號會改變一切。
lessons.big_idea_en: On a staff, higher on the page means higher in pitch. A clef at the start says which note a line is, and the rest follow in alphabetical order, up the lines and spaces.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 在五線譜上，畫得越高，音就越高。開頭的譜號說明哪一條線是哪個音，其餘的就照著字母順序，沿著線和間往上排。

lab.how_en: Tap or click any line or space, even above and below the five lines. A note appears there, you hear it, and you see its name, its solfège name, and its frequency. The keys below show the same note on a keyboard. Switch the clef, and watch what happens to the same note.
lab.how_zh: 在任何一條線或一個間上點一下，甚至在五線的上方和下方。音符會出現在那裡，你會聽到它，也會看到它的音名、唱名和頻率。下面的琴鍵顯示同一個音在鍵盤上的位置。換一個譜號，看看同一個音怎麼變。

paras: Writing needs letters, and music needs a way to write too. A composer who writes a tune on paper must tell a player which notes to play, and how high or low each one is. Over many centuries, people found a simple idea: put the notes on a ladder. The higher a note sits on the page, the higher its pitch.

That ladder is the staff. It is made of five horizontal lines with four spaces between them. A note can sit on a line, or in a space. We count the lines from the bottom: the first line is the lowest. In British English the staff is usually called a stave.

But which note is which line? That is the job of the clef, the symbol at the beginning. The treble clef is also called the G clef. Its curl goes around the second line, and tells you that this line is G4, the G above middle C. The bass clef is also called the F clef. Its two dots sit above and below the fourth line, and tell you that this line is F3. These shapes began as the letters G and F, and became stylized over time.

Once you know one line, you know them all. Notes go up in alphabetical order, through the letters A to G, and then start again. On the treble clef the lines, from the bottom, are E, G, B, D, F, and the spaces are F, A, C, E. Many students remember them as “Every Good Boy Does Fine” and “FACE.” On the bass clef the lines are G, B, D, F, A, and the spaces are A, C, E, G. If a note is above or below the staff, we add a short extra line, called a ledger line.

Middle C shows how clefs work together. It sits one ledger line below the treble staff, and also one ledger line above the bass staff. It is the same note, the same C4, written in two places. In Taiwan, many schools sing notes with the names Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, Si. The English letter names C, D, E, F, G, A, B go with them. A letter name is repeated in every octave, because notes an octave apart share a name.

The names Do, Re, Mi came from a hymn. In the eleventh century in Italy, a music teacher named Guido of Arezzo named the notes of a six-note pattern after the first syllables of the lines of a Latin hymn, “Ut queant laxis.” Later, “Ut” was replaced by the easier “Do.” Some systems keep Do fixed on C, which is called fixed do. Others move Do to the first note of any key, which is called movable do. Taiwan’s school music also uses numbers, 1 to 7, in a notation called jianpu. It writes the same notes as the staff, and both appear in the curriculum.
paras_zh: 寫文字需要字母，寫音樂也需要一種寫法。作曲家把旋律寫在紙上，要告訴演奏的人彈哪些音，每個音有多高或多低。經過許多個世紀，人們找到一個簡單的辦法：把音符放在一座梯子上。音符在紙上畫得越高，音高就越高。
這座梯子就是五線譜（staff）。它由五條水平的線和線與線之間的四個間組成。音符可以在線上，也可以在間裡。線從下面數起：第一線是最低的。英國英文通常把五線譜叫做 stave。
可是哪一條線是哪個音？這是開頭那個符號——譜號（clef）的工作。高音譜號也叫 G 譜號，它的捲曲圈住第二線，說明這條線是 G4，也就是中央 C 上面的那個 G。低音譜號也叫 F 譜號，它的兩個點夾住第四線，說明這條線是 F3。這些形狀原來是 G 和 F 兩個字母，後來慢慢變成了圖案。
只要知道一條線，其他的就都知道了。音依字母順序往上走，A 到 G，然後再從頭開始。高音譜號從下往上的五條線是 E、G、B、D、F，四個間是 F、A、C、E。很多學生用「Every Good Boy Does Fine」和「FACE」來記。低音譜號的線是 G、B、D、F、A，間是 A、C、E、G。如果音在五線的上方或下方，就加一小段短線，叫做加線（ledger line）。
中央 C 最能看出兩個譜號怎麼合作。它在高音譜號的下方加一線上，也在低音譜號的上方加一線上。同一個音、同一個 C4，寫在兩個地方。在台灣，很多學校用 Do、Re、Mi、Fa、Sol、La、Si 唱音，英文字母音名 C、D、E、F、G、A、B 和它們對應。字母名稱在每一個八度裡重複，因為相差八度的音共用同一個名字。

Do、Re、Mi 這些名字來自一首讚美詩。十一世紀的義大利，音樂老師圭多（Guido of Arezzo）用拉丁文讚美詩〈Ut queant laxis〉每一行的第一個音節，替一組六個音命名。後來「Ut」被比較好唱的「Do」取代。有的系統讓 Do 固定在 C 上，叫固定唱名法；有的系統讓 Do 跟著任何調的第一個音走，叫首調唱名法。台灣的學校音樂也用數字 1 到 7 的記譜法，叫簡譜。它寫的是和五線譜同樣的音，兩種寫法都出現在課綱裡。
questions: Why do we need a clef at the beginning of a staff?
A note sits on the first line of a treble staff. Which note is it? What about the first line of a bass staff?
Is middle C in the treble clef a different note from middle C in the bass clef?
answers: The five lines and four spaces are only positions. A clef names the note on one line, and then all the other lines and spaces follow from it.
On the treble staff the first line is E4. On the bass staff the first line is G2. The same position means different notes in different clefs.
No. It is the same note, C4, 261.63 Hz. In the treble clef it is written on a ledger line below the staff, and in the bass clef on a ledger line above it.

vocab.ex: The notes are written on a staff of five lines.
vocab.exzh: 音符寫在有五條線的五線譜上。

vocab.ex: A clef tells you which note each line is.
vocab.exzh: 譜號告訴你每一條線是哪個音。

vocab.ex: Flutes and violins usually read the treble clef.
vocab.exzh: 長笛和小提琴通常讀高音譜號。

vocab.ex: The left hand of the piano often reads the bass clef.
vocab.exzh: 鋼琴的左手常讀低音譜號。

vocab.ex: Middle C sits on a ledger line below the treble staff.
vocab.exzh: 中央 C 在高音譜表下方的加線上。

vocab.ex: This note is in the second space, between two lines.
vocab.exzh: 這個音在第二個間裡，在兩條線之間。

vocab.ex: A higher position on the staff means a higher pitch.
vocab.exzh: 在五線譜上位置越高，音高越高。

vocab.ex: Do, Re, and Mi are each one syllable.
vocab.exzh: Do、Re、Mi 各是一個音節。

quiz.q: How many lines does a staff usually have?
The curl of the treble clef goes around which line, and which note is it?
What are the four spaces of the treble staff, from the bottom?
Where is middle C written in the treble clef?
options: On a ledger line below the staff

quiz.q: In fixed do, which note is always called Do?
options: The first note of any key

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.en: Higher on the page, higher in pitch
parts.text_en: Watch a note climb the staff, one step at a time. Each step is higher in pitch.
parts.text_zh: 看一個音符沿著五線譜一格一格往上爬。每一格的音都更高。

parts.meta_en: The same position, a different note
parts.text_en: The note on the first line is E4 with the treble clef, and G2 with the bass clef.
parts.text_zh: 第一線上的音，在高音譜號是 E4，在低音譜號是 G2。

parts.zh: 中央 C，兩個譜號共用的音
parts.meta_en: A ledger line below, or above
parts.text_en: The same C4 is written under the treble staff and above the bass staff.
parts.text_zh: 同一個 C4，寫在高音譜表的下面，也寫在低音譜表的上面。

parts.text_en: Count up seven positions, lines and spaces together. You land on the same letter, an octave higher.
parts.text_zh: 把線和間一起算，往上數七格。你會落在同一個字母，高一個八度。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the keyboard row under the staff: tap a key, and the note appears on the staff.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試五線譜下面那排琴鍵：點一個鍵，音符就出現在五線譜上。

staffq.lead_en: Eight questions, switching between the treble clef and the bass clef. Look at where the note sits, find a line or space that you know, and count up or down from it. Choose the letter name. The game counts the questions you get right on the first try.
staffq.lead_zh: 八道題，高音譜號和低音譜號輪流出現。看音符的位置，找一條你認得的線或間，從那裡往上或往下數，選出字母音名。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: Reading music is named directly in the curriculum from grades 3 and 4. The curriculum mentions the staff, solfège names, and jianpu, but it does not say whether to use fixed do or movable do.
curric.lead_zh: 讀譜從國小三、四年級起就直接寫在課綱裡。課綱提到五線譜、唱名法和簡譜，但沒有說要用固定唱名法還是首調唱名法。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 讀譜方式，如：五線譜、唱名法、拍號等。
items.note_en: The staff and solfège names are both named as ways of reading music.
items.note_zh: 五線譜和唱名法都被列為讀譜的方式。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 音樂符號與讀譜方式，如：音樂術語、唱名法等。記譜法，如：圖形譜、簡譜、五線譜等。
items.note_en: Three kinds of notation are named: graphic notation, jianpu, and the staff.
items.note_zh: 三種記譜法被點名：圖形譜、簡譜、五線譜。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國中）
items.text: 音樂符號與術語、記譜法或簡易音樂軟體。
items.note_en: In junior high, notation and simple music software come together.
items.note_zh: 國中階段，記譜法和簡易音樂軟體並列。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Staff · 五線譜背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A hymn, a ladder, two letters, and a row of numbers
culture_cards.title_zh: 一首讚美詩、一座梯子、兩個字母，和一排數字
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how music came to be written down.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於音樂怎麼被寫下來的四個小故事。

cards.en: Where Do, Re, Mi came from
cards.body_en: In eleventh-century Italy, the music theorist Guido of Arezzo named the six notes of a pattern after the first syllable of each line of a Latin hymn to St. John: ut, re, mi, fa, sol, la. Each line of the hymn begins one step higher than the last, so singers could remember each note by its line. Later “ut” was changed to the easier “do.” Sources disagree about who changed it and when, so we only say that it happened.
cards.body_zh: 十一世紀的義大利，音樂理論家圭多（Guido of Arezzo）用一首獻給聖約翰的拉丁文讚美詩，每一行的第一個音節，替一組六個音命名：ut、re、mi、fa、sol、la。這首詩每一行的開頭都比上一行高一階，歌者就可以靠那一行詩記住那個音。後來「ut」被改成比較好唱的「do」。各處資料對誰改的、什麼時候改的說法不一，所以我們只說有這回事。

cards.en: A staff that grew from four lines to five
cards.body_en: The modern use of staff lines is attributed to Guido of Arezzo, whose four-line staff is still used in chant books today. Five-line staves appeared in Italy in the 13th century. Staves with four, five, and six lines were all used as late as about 1600. The five-line staff we know became the standard only after that.
cards.body_zh: 現代使用的譜線，歸功於圭多，他的四線譜到今天仍用在聖歌集裡。五線譜在十三世紀出現在義大利。一直到大約 1600 年，四線、五線、六線的譜都還有人用。我們熟悉的五線譜，是在那之後才成為標準。

cards.body_en: At first, a staff had a letter written at its beginning to show which line it named. Over time the shapes of these letters became stylized. The treble clef comes from G, and its curl circles the G line. The bass clef comes from F, and its two dots sit around the F line. There is also a third kind, the C clef, used for the viola and some other instruments.
cards.body_zh: 一開始，五線譜的開頭是直接寫一個字母，表示那一條線的名字。隨著時間，這些字母的形狀變得圖案化。高音譜號來自 G，它的捲曲圈住 G 線；低音譜號來自 F，它的兩個點夾住 F 線。還有第三種，C 譜號，中提琴和一些其他樂器會用到。

cards.k: A Row of Numbers · 一排數字
cards.body_en: Instead of a staff, numbered notation writes the notes of a scale as the numbers 1 to 7, which stand for Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, Si. A dot above a number means an octave higher, and a dot below means an octave lower. Rousseau presented a similar idea to the French Academy of Sciences in 1742, and the Galin–Paris–Chevé system developed it. It came to China by way of Japan around the turn of the twentieth century.
cards.body_zh: 簡譜不用五線，而是把音階的音寫成數字 1 到 7，它們代表 Do、Re、Mi、Fa、Sol、La、Si。數字上方加一點是高八度，下方加一點是低八度。盧梭在 1742 年向法國科學院提出類似的想法，後來由加林—帕里斯—謝韋（Galin–Paris–Chevé）體系發展它。它大約在十九世紀末二十世紀初，經由日本傳到中國。

myths.myth_en: A position on the staff always has the same note name.
myths.myth_zh: 五線譜上的同一個位置，永遠是同一個音名。
myths.fact_en: The clef decides. The first line is E4 in the treble clef, and G2 in the bass clef. Without a clef, a staff is only a set of positions.
myths.fact_zh: 由譜號決定。第一線在高音譜號是 E4，在低音譜號是 G2。沒有譜號，五線譜只是一組位置。

myths.myth_en: Middle C is a different note in the treble and bass clefs.
myths.myth_zh: 中央 C 在高音譜號和低音譜號是不同的音。
myths.fact_en: It is the same note, C4. It sits on a ledger line below the treble staff, and on a ledger line above the bass staff.
myths.fact_zh: 它是同一個音，C4。它在高音譜表下方的加線上，也在低音譜表上方的加線上。

myths.myth_en: Do always means the note C.
myths.myth_zh: Do 永遠就是 C 這個音。
myths.fact_en: Only in fixed do. In movable do, Do is the first note of whatever key the music is in. The curriculum names “solfège” but does not choose between them.
myths.fact_zh: 只有固定唱名法是這樣。首調唱名法裡，Do 是這首音樂所在調的第一個音。課綱只寫「唱名法」，沒有在兩者之間選一個。

myths.myth_en: Do, Re, Mi were made up to teach children.
myths.myth_zh: Do、Re、Mi 是為了教小朋友才編出來的。
myths.fact_en: They come from the first syllables of the lines of a Latin hymn, and they were in use in the eleventh century in Italy. Teachers have used them to teach singing for about a thousand years.
myths.fact_zh: 它們來自一首拉丁文讚美詩每一行的第一個音節，十一世紀的義大利就在用。老師用它們教唱歌，已經差不多一千年。

tricks_head.en: Reading the staff in a sentence

tricks.title_en: Higher on the page, higher in pitch
tricks.body_en: The staff is a ladder for pitch.
tricks.body_zh: 五線譜是音高的梯子。

tricks.title_en: Treble lines: E G B D F; spaces: F A C E
tricks.title_zh: 高音譜號：線 E G B D F、間 F A C E
tricks.body_en: Every Good Boy Does Fine, and FACE.
tricks.body_zh: Every Good Boy Does Fine，還有 FACE。

tricks.body_en: Lines and spaces together: seven steps up is one octave.
tricks.body_zh: 線和間一起算：往上七格是一個八度。

tricks.title_en: Middle C lives between the two staffs
tricks.title_zh: 中央 C 住在兩個譜表中間
tricks.body_en: One ledger line below the treble, or above the bass.
tricks.body_zh: 高音譜表下方一條加線，或低音譜表上方一條加線。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: Tap the screen with a fingertip. You do not need to press hard, and do not tap the screen with a pen or any hard object.
safety.zh: 用指尖點螢幕就好，不需要用力，也不要用筆或硬的東西敲螢幕。

materials.en: Five long strips of masking tape or five ropes
materials.zh: 五條長長的紙膠帶或五條繩子

materials.en: A large card with a clef drawn on it
materials.zh: 一張畫了譜號的大卡片

materials.en: Cards with the letters C D E F G A B
materials.zh: 寫了 C D E F G A B 的卡片

steps.en: Lay the five strips on the floor, about one big step apart, to make a staff. Put the treble clef card at the left end.
steps.zh: 把五條帶子鋪在地上，每條相隔大約一步，做成五線譜。把高音譜號的卡片放在左端。

steps.en: One student stands on a line or in a space. The class says the note name. The student with the keyboard, or the page, plays it to check.
steps.zh: 一位同學站在一條線上或一個間裡。全班說出音名。拿著鍵盤或用本頁的同學彈出來核對。

steps.en: Move the clef card to a bass clef card. Does the same place have the same name?
steps.zh: 把譜號卡片換成低音譜號的卡片。同一個位置還是同一個名字嗎？

steps.en: Let a student stand one step above the top line. How many ledger lines does that note need?
steps.zh: 讓一位同學站在最上面那條線再往上一格的地方。這個音需要幾條加線？

activities.tip_en: Walk, do not run, and keep the strips taped down so nobody slips.
activities.tip_zh: 用走的，不要跑，帶子要貼牢，免得有人滑倒。

materials.en: A sheet of paper with a staff drawn on it
Five small coins or buttons
A keyboard, recorder, or the page on this screen
materials.zh: 一個鍵盤、直笛，或這個螢幕上的頁面

steps.en: Draw five lines on the paper, evenly spaced, and write a treble clef on the left.
steps.zh: 在紙上畫五條間隔均勻的線，並在左邊寫一個高音譜號。

steps.en: Put the coins on the lines and spaces to make a short tune, and write the letter names under them.
steps.zh: 把硬幣放在線和間上，做成一小段旋律，並在下面寫出字母音名。

steps.en: Play the tune on the page or an instrument, from the letters. Does it sound the way you pictured it?
steps.zh: 照著字母，在頁面或樂器上把旋律彈出來。聽起來和你想的一樣嗎？

steps.en: Swap papers with a partner and play each other’s tunes.
steps.zh: 和同伴交換紙，彼此演奏對方的旋律。

activities.tip_en: Use only notes between the lowest and the highest line at first. Add a ledger line only after you can read the staff itself.
activities.tip_zh: 一開始只用最低線到最高線之間的音。等你會讀五線以後，再加加線。

links_head.en: Before, around, and after this lesson
links_head.zh: 這一課的前面、旁邊和後面

links.en: How Do You Tell a Musician “Louder” or “Faster”?
links.zh: 怎麼告訴演奏的人「大聲一點」「快一點」？
links.note_en: Signs such as p, f, and allegro are written on the staff, together with the notes.
links.note_zh: p、f、allegro 這些記號，就和音符一起寫在五線譜上。

links.en: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
links.zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
links.note_en: That lesson gave the letter names and frequencies: A4 is 440 Hz, and C4 is 261.63 Hz.
links.note_zh: 那一課給了字母音名和頻率：A4 是 440 赫、C4 是 261.63 赫。

links.en: How Long Is a Note?
links.note_en: The staff shows how high a note is. The next lesson shows how long: note values and the time signature.
links.note_zh: 五線譜顯示音有多高；下一課顯示音有多長：音符的時值和拍號。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The note positions are computed by the page itself and covered by automatic tests. The clef shapes on the page are our own simplified drawings.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；音符的位置由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試。頁面上的譜號是我們自己畫的簡化圖形。

sources.en: The staff: a set of horizontal lines (usually five) with spaces between them; higher notes are marked higher; ledger lines; UK usually stave; history (Guido's four-line staff, five lines in the 13th century, four to six lines as late as 1600)
sources.zh: 五線譜：一組水平的線（通常五條）和之間的間；越高的音畫得越高；加線；英國通常叫 stave；歷史（圭多的四線譜、十三世紀的五線、直到 1600 年前後仍有四到六線）

sources.en: A ledger line is spaced at the same distance as the lines within the staff and is used for pitches above or below the staff
sources.zh: 加線的間距和譜線相同，用來寫五線上方或下方的音

sources.en: Clefs: G, F, and C; the treble clef places G4 on the second line and the bass clef F3 on the fourth line; the clef shapes are stylized letters; the mnemonics Every Good Boy Does Fine and FACE
sources.zh: 譜號：G、F、C 三種；高音譜號把 G4 放在第二線、低音譜號把 F3 放在第四線；譜號的形狀是圖案化的字母；口訣 Every Good Boy Does Fine 與 FACE

sources.en: Middle C is C4; it sits one ledger line below the treble staff or one ledger line above the bass staff; pitch classes use the letters A to G
sources.zh: 中央 C 是 C4；它在高音譜表下方一條加線或低音譜表上方一條加線；音級用字母 A 到 G

sources.en: Guido of Arezzo named the notes after the first syllables of the lines of “Ut queant laxis”; fixed do and movable do
sources.zh: 圭多用〈Ut queant laxis〉每行的第一個音節為音命名；固定唱名法與首調唱名法

sources.en: The hymn “Ut queant laxis”: each line begins one step higher
sources.zh: 讚美詩〈Ut queant laxis〉：每一行的開頭都高一階

sources.en: Numbered musical notation: Rousseau's similar proposal of 1742; the Galin–Paris–Chevé system; introduced in Japan and then adopted in China
sources.zh: 數字簡譜：盧梭 1742 年類似的提案；Galin–Paris–Chevé 體系；先傳入日本、再被中國採用

sources.en: 譜號: the clef is marked at the front of the staff; the treble clef (G clef) is on the second line, which is g′
sources.zh: 譜號：標在五線譜最前端；高音譜號（G 譜號）記在第二線上，表示該線上的音為 g′
sources.src: 教育百科〈譜號〉（國教院《舞蹈辭典》）

sources.en: 五線譜: five parallel lines, called the first to the fifth line, and the first to the fourth space, from the bottom
sources.zh: 五線譜：五根平行橫線，自下而上稱為第一線到第五線，以及第一間到第四間
sources.src: 教育百科〈五線譜〉（國教院《舞蹈辭典》）

sources.en: 簡譜: numbers 1 to 7 for Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, Si; a dot above or below marks an octave higher or lower
sources.zh: 簡譜：以 1 到 7 表示 Do、Re、Mi、Fa、Sol、La、Si；數字上方或下方加點表示高八度或低八度
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「簡譜」

sources.en: 五線譜, 譜號, 音名 in the Ministry of Education Dictionary
sources.zh: 教育部辭典「五線譜」「譜號」「音名」

lessons.title: How Long Is a Note?
lessons.blurb_en: Fill a bar with note blocks until it is exactly full, then see it on a staff and hear it. Find out why every note is half as long as the one before it.
lessons.blurb_zh: 用音符積木把一小節剛好填滿，再看它寫在五線譜上、聽它播出來。看看為什麼每個音符都是前一個的一半長。
lessons.big_idea_en: Note lengths keep getting cut in half: a whole note, then two half notes, four quarter notes, eight eighth notes. A time signature says how many beats fit in a bar, and a bar must be filled exactly.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 音符的長度一路對半分：一個全音符，是兩個二分音符、四個四分音符、八個八分音符。拍號說每小節裡放得下幾拍，而一小節要剛好填滿。

lab.how_en: Choose a time signature, then press the note buttons to add notes one at a time. The strip shows how long each note is, and the staff shows how it is written. A note that does not fit is turned away, and it tells you how many beats are left. Add a dot to make a note one and a half times as long, or switch on Rest to add silence. When the bar is full, press play.
lab.how_zh: 選一個拍號，再按音符按鈕，一次加一個音符。長條顯示每個音符多長，五線譜顯示它怎麼寫。放不下的音符會被擋下來，並告訴你還剩幾拍。加上附點，音符就變成一又二分之一倍長；打開「休止符」就加上一段安靜。小節填滿了，就按播放。

paras: Last time you learned where to put a note on the staff to show how high it is. But a note also needs to say how long it lasts. The answer is in its shape. A note value tells us the relative length of a note by the look of its head, whether it has a stem, and whether it has flags or beams.

The idea is easy to remember: each note is half as long as the one before it. A whole note is a hollow oval with no stem. Two half notes, which have a stem, fit in the time of one whole note. Four quarter notes, with filled heads, fit in the same time. Eight eighth notes, which have one flag each, and sixteen sixteenth notes, which have two, do too. In the United States we use these names. In British English they are called semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, and semiquaver.

How long is a quarter note in seconds? It depends on the tempo. A note value is relative. At 60 beats per minute, a quarter note lasts one second. At 120 beats per minute, it lasts half a second. In music we count beats, and a quarter note is one beat when the bottom number of the time signature is 4. So a half note gets two beats, and a whole note gets four.

A dot after a note makes it longer by half of its own value. A half note is two beats, so a dotted half note is two plus one, three beats. A dotted quarter note is one and a half beats. There are rests, too. A rest is the absence of sound for a set length of time, and each kind is named for the note value it matches. A quarter rest lasts as long as a quarter note, and it is silent.

Now we can understand the time signature. In 4/4, the top number says there are four beats in each bar, and the bottom number says that a quarter note is one beat. So a bar of 4/4 can hold one whole note, or two half notes, or four quarter notes, or a half note and two quarter notes. In 3/4, it holds three beats. The notes of a bar must add up exactly. That is the puzzle that composers solve in every bar.

Notes with different lengths make rhythm. Taiwan’s school music also uses jianpu, the numbered notation, and it has its own signs for length. A short line after a number makes it longer, a line under a number makes it half as long, and a circle is a rest. The same ideas of halves and halves again are there too. Whichever way it is written, the relative length is what matters, and the tempo decides how many seconds it lasts.
paras_zh: 上一課你學到在五線譜上把音放在哪裡，可以表示音有多高。可是一個音也要說明它持續多久。答案就在它的形狀裡。「音符時值」是靠符頭的樣子、有沒有符桿、有沒有符尾或符槓，來說明音符的相對長度。
這個想法很好記：每個音符都是前一個的一半長。全音符是沒有符桿的空心橢圓；兩個有符桿的二分音符，剛好等於一個全音符的時間；四個符頭是實心的四分音符，也是同樣的時間；八個各有一條符尾的八分音符，和十六個各有兩條符尾的十六分音符，也一樣。美國用這些名稱；英國英文則叫 semibreve、minim、crotchet、quaver、semiquaver。
四分音符有幾秒長？要看速度。音符時值是相對的。每分鐘 60 拍時，四分音符長一秒；每分鐘 120 拍時，長半秒。在音樂裡我們數拍，拍號下面的數字是 4 的時候，一個四分音符就是一拍。所以二分音符是兩拍，全音符是四拍。
音符後面加一個點，就會多出它自己一半的長度。二分音符是兩拍，所以附點二分音符是二加一，共三拍；附點四分音符是一又二分之一拍。也有休止符：它是一段固定長度的沉默，每一種都用它對應的音符時值來命名。四分休止符和四分音符一樣長，只是沒有聲音。
現在我們可以懂拍號了。在 4/4 裡，上面的數字說每小節有四拍，下面的數字說以四分音符為一拍。所以一個 4/4 的小節，可以放一個全音符、或兩個二分音符、或四個四分音符，或一個二分音符加兩個四分音符。在 3/4 裡，放三拍。一小節裡的音符，加起來要剛剛好。這就是作曲家在每個小節裡都要解的謎題。
長短不同的音符組成節奏。台灣的學校音樂也用簡譜（數字記譜），它有自己表示長短的記號：數字後面加一條短橫線，就變長；數字底下加一條線，就變成一半；圓圈則是休止符。同樣是一半再一半的想法。不管怎麼寫，要緊的是相對的長短，速度才決定它是幾秒。
questions: How many eighth notes fit in one half note?
A bar in 3/4 has a dotted half note. What else fits in the bar?
Is a quarter note always one second long? Why or why not?
answers: Four. A half note is two beats, and an eighth note is half a beat, so 2 ÷ ½ = 4.
Nothing else. A dotted half note is 3 beats, and a bar of 3/4 holds 3 beats, so it is full.
No. A note value is relative. A quarter note is one beat, and how long a beat lasts depends on the tempo. At 60 BPM it is one second, and at 120 BPM it is half a second.

vocab.ex: A half note has a longer note value than a quarter note.
vocab.exzh: 二分音符的時值比四分音符長。

vocab.ex: A whole note lasts four beats in 4/4.
vocab.exzh: 全音符在 4/4 裡長四拍。

vocab.ex: A quarter note usually gets one beat.
vocab.exzh: 四分音符通常是一拍。

vocab.ex: Count one beat for the rest, and do not play.
vocab.exzh: 休止符數一拍，不要演奏。

vocab.ex: A dot makes a note half again as long.
vocab.exzh: 附點會讓音符再多出一半的長度。

vocab.ex: Each bar of this song has four beats.
vocab.exzh: 這首歌的每一小節有四拍。

vocab.ex: A half note has a stem, and a whole note does not.
vocab.exzh: 二分音符有符桿，全音符沒有。

vocab.ex: An eighth note has one flag on its stem.
vocab.exzh: 八分音符的符桿上有一條符尾。

What does a dot after a note do?
options: Makes it half as long again

quiz.q: In 4/4, how many beats does a dotted half note get?
What is a rest?

The last note of a bar

quiz.q: A bar of 3/4 is filled by…
options: A half note and a quarter note

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: These four blocks add up to exactly four beats. Watch the strip fill, and hear the bar.
parts.text_zh: 這四塊加起來剛好四拍。看長條被填滿，並聽這一小節。

parts.text_en: A dotted half note and a quarter note fill a bar of 4/4.
parts.text_zh: 一個附點二分音符加一個四分音符，填滿 4/4 的小節。

parts.en: A rest is silent but counts
parts.zh: 休止符沒有聲音，但要算
parts.text_en: Listen for the gap in the middle of the bar. The beat clicks go on through it.
parts.text_zh: 聽小節中間的空隙。節拍的喀喀聲照常走過去。

parts.text_en: Switch the time signature, and the same notes make a different bar.
parts.text_zh: 換一個拍號，同樣的音符就組成不一樣的小節。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself: can you fill a 4/4 bar using at least three different note values?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己試試：你能不能用至少三種不同的音符時值，填滿一個 4/4 的小節？

split.lead_en: Every row fills the same four beats. The first row uses one note, the second uses two, and so on, doubling each time. Press a row and listen to how the notes get closer together.
split.lead_zh: 每一列都填滿同樣的四拍。第一列用一個音，第二列用兩個，一直倍增下去。按一列，聽聽音符怎麼越來越密。

beatq.lead_en: Eight questions, all in 4/4. Each one shows a note or a rest, and you choose how many beats it lasts. The game counts the questions you get right on the first try.
beatq.lead_zh: 八道題，全部在 4/4 裡。每一題給你看一個音符或休止符，你選它占幾拍。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names rhythm and time signatures, and it also names simple composing. The words “note” and “rest” do not appear in the curriculum itself.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱寫到節奏和拍號，也寫到簡易創作。「音符」和「休止」這兩個詞，課綱本文裡沒有出現。

items.note_zh: 節奏是被點名的第一個音樂元素。

items.note_en: Notation systems, including jianpu and the staff, are named.
items.note_zh: 記譜法被點名，包括簡譜和五線譜。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 簡易創作，如：節奏創作、曲調創作、曲式創作等。
items.note_en: Filling a bar with your own mix of notes and rests is a small piece of rhythm composing.
items.note_zh: 用你自己選的音符和休止符填滿一小節，就是一小段節奏創作。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Names, a dot, a silence, and a row of numbers
culture_cards.title_zh: 名字、一個點、一段安靜，和一排數字
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how music writes down length.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於音樂怎麼把長短寫下來的四個小故事。

cards.en: Whole, half, quarter: a German loan
cards.zh: 全、二分、四分：從德文借來的
cards.body_en: The American names are translations of German ones. The American whole note is a calque of the German ganze Note, and the quarter note follows the German Viertelnote. The British names are older and come from other places. Crotchet is from an Old French word for a little hook, named after the shape of the note, and minim comes from the Latin for very small.
cards.body_zh: 美式名稱是從德文翻譯來的。美式的 whole note 是德文 ganze Note 的直譯，quarter note 也來自德文 Viertelnote。英式名稱比較古老，來自別的地方：crotchet 來自古法文的「小鉤子」，是依音符的形狀命名；minim 來自拉丁文的「很小」。

cards.en: A dot, and a double dot
cards.body_en: A single dot adds half of the note's value. A second dot adds half of that again, so a double-dotted note lasts 1¾ times its basic value. For instance, a double-dotted half note is 2 + 1 + ½ = 3½ beats. Double dots were not used until the middle of the 18th century.
cards.body_zh: 一個點加上音符時值的一半。第二個點再加上那一半的一半，所以複附點音符的長度是原時值的 1¾ 倍。例如複附點二分音符是 2＋1＋½＝3½ 拍。複附點直到十八世紀中葉才有人用。

cards.body_en: A rest is the absence of sound for a defined length of time, and each kind is named for the note value it matches. There are rests for every note value, from the whole rest to the thirty-second rest. One special case: when a whole bar is silent, a whole rest is used, whatever the time signature is. So a whole rest does not always mean four beats.
cards.body_zh: 休止符是一段有明確長度的沒有聲音，每一種都用它對應的音符時值命名。從全休止符到三十二分休止符，每一種時值都有休止符。有一個特別的情況：整個小節都沒有聲音時，不管拍號是什麼，都用全休止符。所以全休止符不一定是四拍。

cards.k: A Row of Numbers · 一排數字
cards.body_en: In jianpu, each number is worth a quarter note. A dash after a number makes it twice as long, like a half note. A line under a number cuts it in half, like an eighth note. A rest is written with a circle. The time signature is written as two numbers, such as 3/4, in the same way as on the staff.
cards.body_zh: 在簡譜裡，每個數字相當於五線譜的四分音符。數字後面加一條短橫線，長度加倍，相當於二分音符；數字底下加一條線，長度減半，相當於八分音符；休止符用圓圈寫。拍號和五線譜一樣，寫成兩個數字，例如 3/4。

myths.myth_en: A whole note always lasts four seconds.
myths.myth_zh: 全音符永遠是四秒。
myths.fact_en: A note value is relative. A whole note is four beats when a quarter note is one beat, and the number of seconds depends on the tempo. At 60 BPM it is four seconds. At 120 BPM it is two.
myths.fact_zh: 音符時值是相對的。當四分音符是一拍時，全音符是四拍，幾秒要看速度：60 BPM 是四秒，120 BPM 是兩秒。

myths.myth_en: A rest means nothing happens.
myths.myth_zh: 休止符就是什麼都不發生。
myths.fact_en: A rest is silent but it takes time. It keeps the rhythm going, and the player must count it.
myths.fact_zh: 休止符沒有聲音，但它占時間。它讓節奏繼續走，演奏的人必須數它。

myths.myth_en: A whole rest is always four beats.
myths.myth_zh: 全休止符永遠是四拍。
myths.fact_en: A whole rest is used for a whole silent bar, in any time signature. In 3/4 a whole rest means three beats.
myths.fact_zh: 全休止符用來表示整個沒有聲音的小節，不管什麼拍號。在 3/4 裡，全休止符是三拍。

myths.myth_en: A dot just makes a note longer by one beat.
myths.myth_zh: 附點只是讓音符多一拍。
myths.fact_en: A dot adds half of the note's own value. For a half note that is one beat, for a quarter note it is half a beat, and for an eighth note it is a quarter of a beat.
myths.fact_zh: 附點加上音符自己時值的一半：二分音符加一拍、四分音符加半拍、八分音符加四分之一拍。

tricks.body_en: Whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth.
tricks.body_zh: 全、二分、四分、八分、十六分。

tricks.body_en: Dotted half = 2 + 1 = 3 beats.
tricks.body_zh: 附點二分＝2＋1＝3 拍。

tricks.title_en: A rest is silent but counted
tricks.body_en: Same length as the note of the same name.
tricks.body_zh: 和同名的音符一樣長。

tricks.body_en: 4/4 holds four quarter notes' worth.
tricks.body_zh: 4/4 放得下四個四分音符的長度。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: When you clap or tap rhythms in class, use soft hands or a pad, and do not clap close to anyone’s ears.
safety.zh: 在課堂上拍或敲節奏時，用軟軟的手或墊子，不要在別人耳朵旁邊拍手。

materials.en: Paper strips, each one the same length, for the whole class
materials.zh: 全班每人一條一樣長的紙條

materials.en: Pencils
The page, for a steady beat

steps.en: Fold the strip in half, then in half again, and again, like folding paper into halves, quarters, and eighths. Mark the folds.
steps.zh: 把紙條對摺、再對摺、再對摺，就像把紙摺成二分之一、四分之一、八分之一。把摺痕標出來。

steps.en: Let the whole strip be one bar of four beats. Clap one clap for the whole strip, then two claps for halves, four for quarters, and eight for eighths, all in the same four beats.
steps.zh: 把整條紙條當作四拍的一小節。整條拍一下，二分之一各拍一下共兩下，四分之一共四下，八分之一共八下，全都在同樣的四拍裡。

steps.en: Write the claps on the strip as notes: whole, half, quarter, eighth.
steps.zh: 把拍手的次數在紙條上寫成音符：全音符、二分音符、四分音符、八分音符。

steps.en: Now clap a pattern of your own that fills the strip. Your partner reads it back.
steps.zh: 再拍一個你自己的圖樣，填滿紙條。同伴把它讀回來。

activities.tip_en: Second graders already learn halves, quarters, and eighths of folded paper in math class, so the same idea is a good start for note values.
activities.tip_zh: 二年級的數學課就用摺紙認識二分之一、四分之一和八分之一，所以同樣的想法是學音符時值的好開頭。

materials.en: An open space in the classroom
Cards with notes and rests: quarter note, quarter rest, half note, half rest
materials.zh: 寫了音符和休止符的卡片：四分音符、四分休止符、二分音符、二分休止符

materials.en: The metronome from lesson 3 at 80 BPM
materials.zh: 第三課的節拍器，速度 80 BPM

steps.en: Everyone steps in place on every beat. The teacher shows a card.
steps.zh: 大家在每一拍原地踏步。老師出示一張卡片。

steps.en: For a note card, clap once and hold the clap for the length of the note. For a rest card, freeze like a statue for the length of the rest.
steps.zh: 看到音符卡，就拍一下手，並保持到音符那麼長。看到休止符卡，就像雕像一樣靜止，停那麼久。

steps.en: Show a row of four cards, one for each beat, and perform them together.
steps.zh: 出示一排四張卡片，每張一拍，大家一起表演。

steps.en: Let students make their own row for a 4/4 bar, and check that it adds up to four beats.
steps.zh: 讓學生做自己的一排 4/4 小節，並檢查加起來是不是四拍。

activities.tip_en: Keep the stepping light and stay in your own space. The quiet of a rest is part of the music, so listen to it.
activities.tip_zh: 踏步輕輕的，待在自己的位置。休止符的安靜也是音樂的一部分，要聽它。

lessons.title: What Is a Scale?
lessons.blurb_en: Build major, minor, and pentatonic scales one key at a time, and hear the same tune in three different scales. Find out what a whole step and a half step are.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一個鍵一個鍵建出大調、小調和五聲音階，聽同一段旋律換三種音階。看看什麼是全音和半音。
lessons.big_idea_en: A scale is a ladder of notes from low to high. The steps between the notes are whole steps and half steps, and the pattern of those steps decides which scale it is.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 音階是一座由低到高的音的階梯。音和音之間的步階是全音和半音，這些步階的排列圖樣，決定它是哪一種音階。

lab.how_en: Choose a tonic, the note you start on, and a kind of scale. Then press the keys one at a time, following the pattern of whole steps (W) and half steps (H). If you press the wrong key, the page tells you which step comes next. When the scale is built, you can see it on the staff and play it. The tonics here are all white keys, so some scales need black keys: they are shown with a sharp (♯) or a flat (♭).
lab.how_zh: 選一個主音（你開始的那個音）和一種音階，然後依照全音（W）與半音（H）的圖樣，一次按一個鍵。按錯了，頁面會告訴你下一步是什麼。音階建好了，可以在五線譜上看，也可以播放。這裡的主音都是白鍵，所以有些音階需要黑鍵：它們會用升記號（♯）或降記號（♭）標出來。

paras: A scale is a series of notes arranged from low to high, from one note up to the same note an octave higher. The first note is called the tonic. The English word scale comes from the Latin scala, which means ladder, and that is a good picture: every note is a rung, and you climb from the tonic to the top.

The distance between neighboring rungs comes in two sizes. A half step, also called a semitone, is the distance between two neighboring keys on a piano. A whole step is two half steps. In the equal temperament you met in lesson 1, each half step is a frequency ratio of 2 to the power of 1/12, so two half steps multiply the frequency by about 1.12. On the piano, E to F and B to C are half steps, because there is no black key between them.

A major scale has a pattern of seven steps: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. That is W W H W W W H. Start on C and you only need white keys: C D E F G A B C. The two half steps fall between the third and fourth notes, and between the seventh and eighth. In equal temperament, the notes of a major scale are 0, 200, 400, 500, 700, 900, 1100, and 1200 cents above the tonic.

The pattern is what makes the scale, not the starting note. Start on D and keep W W H W W W H, and you must use F♯ and C♯. A sharp raises a note by a half step. A flat lowers it. A natural minor scale has a different pattern: W H W W H W W. Compared with a major scale from the same tonic, its third, sixth, and seventh notes are a half step lower. From A, it uses only white keys: A B C D E F G A.

Many people hear major scales as brighter and minor scales as more serious or sad. Taiwan’s dictionary says a major key usually sounds brighter than a minor one. But research suggests this link is at least partly learned, and it also depends on tempo and context. So try it yourself: play the same tune in both, and describe what you hear in your own words.

Not every scale has seven notes. A pentatonic scale has five notes in an octave. The major pentatonic scale uses the first, second, third, fifth, and sixth notes of a major scale: C D E G A. The five black keys on a piano also make a pentatonic scale. Pentatonic scales are found in many cultures. In Chinese music, the five notes are named gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu, and each of them can be the tonic of its own mode.
paras_zh: 音階是一串由低到高排好的音，從一個音一直排到高八度的同一個音。第一個音叫主音。英文的 scale 來自拉丁文的 scala，意思是梯子，這是很好的畫面：每個音是一格橫木，你從主音往上爬。
相鄰兩格之間的距離有兩種大小。半音（semitone）是鋼琴上相鄰兩個鍵的距離；全音是兩個半音。在你第一課認識的十二平均律裡，每個半音的頻率比是 2 的 1/12 次方，所以兩個半音會把頻率乘上大約 1.12。在鋼琴上，E 到 F、B 到 C 是半音，因為它們之間沒有黑鍵。
大調音階有七個步階的圖樣：全、全、半、全、全、全、半，也就是 W W H W W W H。從 C 開始，只要用白鍵：C D E F G A B C。兩個半音落在第三、四音之間，和第七、八音之間。在十二平均律裡，大調音階各音比主音高 0、200、400、500、700、900、1100、1200 音分。
決定一個音階的是圖樣，不是起點。從 D 開始、維持 W W H W W W H，就必須用 F♯ 和 C♯。升記號把音升高一個半音，降記號把音降低一個半音。自然小調音階的圖樣不同：W H W W H W W。和同一個主音的大調比，它的第三、第六、第七個音各低一個半音。從 A 開始，只用白鍵：A B C D E F G A。
許多人聽大調覺得比較明亮，聽小調覺得比較嚴肅或悲傷。台灣的辭典說，大調的色彩通常比小調明朗。不過研究認為，這種連結至少有一部分是學來的，也和速度與情境有關。所以請你自己試試：同一段旋律用兩種音階各彈一次，用你自己的話形容聽到的。
不是每個音階都有七個音。五聲音階在一個八度裡有五個音。大調五聲音階用大調音階的第一、二、三、五、六音：C D E G A。鋼琴上的五個黑鍵，也組成一個五聲音階。許多文化都有五聲音階。在中國音樂裡，這五個音叫宮、商、角、徵、羽，每一個音都可以當自己那個調式的主音。
questions: In the C major scale, which neighboring notes are a half step apart?
Why does a major scale that starts on D need black keys?
Are the black keys the only pentatonic scale on a piano?
answers: E and F, and B and C. Those are the pairs with no black key between them, and they are the third and fourth notes, and the seventh and eighth notes of the scale.
Because the pattern W W H W W W H must stay the same. Starting on D, the third note has to be F♯, and the seventh note has to be C♯, so two black keys join in.
No. They make one pentatonic scale, F♯ major pentatonic. The white keys C D E G A also make a pentatonic scale, and so do many other groups of five.

tune.lead_en: This short tune goes up the scale and comes back home. The tune is written as “first note, second note, third note…”, so it fits any scale. Press a button, and the tune is played using the notes of that scale.

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A ladder, five tones, a cut pipe, and a world of five notes
culture_cards.title_zh: 一座階梯、五個音、一根被截短的管，和世界各地的五個音
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people have named and built scales.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人們怎麼為音階命名、怎麼建構音階的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: According to Wikipedia, the English word scale comes from the Latin scala, which literally means ladder. Taiwan’s dictionary calls 音階 a translation of the English word scale. Each note is a rung, and the steps between the rungs are not always the same size.
cards.body_zh: 依維基百科，英文 scale 來自拉丁文 scala，字面意思是「梯子」。台灣的辭典說「音階」是英文 scale 的意譯。每個音是一格橫木，而橫木之間的距離並不總是一樣大。

cards.body_en: Taiwan’s dictionary lists the five tones of ancient Chinese music as 宮, 商, 角, 徵, and 羽, and cites the Zuo Zhuan and the Rites of Zhou. A reference entry adds that each of the five tones can serve as the tonic, which gives five different pentatonic modes. They are often matched with Do Re Mi Sol La, but only roughly, because any of the five can be the tonic.
cards.body_zh: 台灣的辭典把中國古代音樂的五音列為宮、商、角、徵、羽，並引用《左傳》和《周禮》。一則辭書條目補充：這五個音每一個都可以當主音，所以有五種不同的五聲調式。它們常被對應到 Do Re Mi Sol La，但只是大致對應，因為五個音都可以當主音。

cards.k: A Cut Pipe · 一根被截短的管
cards.en: Subtract a third, add a third
cards.body_en: Ancient Chinese texts, including the Guanzi and the Lüshi Chunqiu, describe making notes by cutting a length into three parts and either removing one part or adding one. Start with 81. Remove a third and you get 54. Add a third to that and you get 72. Taiwan’s reference entry says this works out the same, mathematically, as the method of Pythagoras in ancient Greece. Removing a third leaves 2/3 of the length, the same 2 : 3 you saw in lesson 1.
cards.body_zh: 中國古代文獻，包括《管子》和《呂氏春秋》，記載把一段長度分成三份，再減去一份或加上一份來生出音。從 81 開始，減去三分之一得到 54；再加上它的三分之一得到 72。台灣的辭書條目說，這在數理上和古希臘畢達哥拉斯的方法相通。減去三分之一，剩下 2/3 的長度，就是第一課看過的 2 比 3。

cards.k: Five Notes Worldwide · 世界各地的五個音
cards.zh: 你可能聽過的五聲音階歌曲
cards.body_en: Wikipedia says pentatonic scales were developed independently by many ancient civilizations. It names the hymn “Amazing Grace” and the Scottish tune of “Auld Lang Syne” as pentatonic melodies. The Chinese folk song “Mo Li Hua” (Jasmine Flower) uses a five-note scale that is common in Chinese music. Try playing them on the black keys.
cards.body_zh: 維基百科說，許多古老的文明各自發展出五聲音階。它舉出聖詩〈Amazing Grace〉和蘇格蘭曲調〈Auld Lang Syne〉是五聲音階的旋律；中國民歌〈茉莉花〉用的是中國音樂裡很常見的五個音的音階。你可以試著用黑鍵彈彈看。

myths.myth_en: Major is happy and minor is sad.
myths.myth_zh: 大調就是快樂，小調就是悲傷。
myths.fact_en: Many listeners hear major as brighter and minor as more serious, but studies suggest the link is at least partly learned, and it depends on tempo and context as well.
myths.fact_zh: 許多聽眾覺得大調較明亮、小調較嚴肅，但研究認為這種連結至少有一部分是學來的，也和速度與情境有關。

myths.myth_en: The black keys are the pentatonic scale.
myths.myth_zh: 黑鍵就是五聲音階。
myths.fact_en: The black keys make one pentatonic scale. The white keys C D E G A make another, and there are many more.
myths.fact_zh: 黑鍵組成的是其中一個五聲音階。白鍵 C D E G A 也是一個，還有很多別的。

myths.myth_en: A scale must have eight notes.
myths.myth_zh: 音階一定有八個音。
myths.fact_en: A major scale has seven different notes, and the eighth is the tonic again. A pentatonic scale has five.
myths.fact_zh: 大調音階有七個不同的音，第八個是再回到主音。五聲音階只有五個。

myths.myth_en: A half step is a note that is half as long.
myths.myth_zh: 半音就是長度只有一半的音。
myths.fact_en: A half step is about pitch, not length. It is the distance between two neighboring piano keys, and a whole step is two half steps.
myths.fact_zh: 半音說的是音高，不是長短。它是鋼琴上相鄰兩個鍵的距離，兩個半音是一個全音。

tricks.body_en: Notes in order, from low to high.
tricks.body_zh: 音依序排好，由低到高。

tricks.body_en: A whole step is two half steps.
tricks.body_zh: 一個全音是兩個半音。

tricks.title_en: Major: W W H W W W H
tricks.body_en: The two half steps sit between 3 and 4, and 7 and 8.
tricks.body_zh: 兩個半音在第 3、4 音之間，和第 7、8 音之間。

tricks.body_en: Natural minor also lowers the sixth and seventh.
tricks.body_zh: 自然小調也降低第六和第七音。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: When you sing or hum a scale, stay in a range that is comfortable. Do not push your voice too high or too loud, and stop if your throat hurts.
safety.zh: 唱或哼音階時，待在舒服的音域裡。不要把聲音勉強唱得太高或太大聲；喉嚨痛就停下來。

materials.en: Eight students, or a row of eight chairs
materials.zh: 八位同學，或排成一排的八張椅子

materials.en: Two sticky notes marked W and H for each gap
materials.zh: 每個空隙兩張標了 W 和 H 的便利貼

materials.en: A keyboard, a xylophone, or this page

steps.en: Students stand in a row and each is one note of C major, from C up to the next C.
steps.zh: 同學排成一列，每個人是 C 大調的一個音，從 C 到上一個 C。

steps.en: Between each pair of neighbors, place a W or an H sticky note, following W W H W W W H.
steps.zh: 在每兩位相鄰的同學之間貼上 W 或 H 的便利貼，依照 全 全 半 全 全 全 半。

steps.en: Sing the scale up, with each student singing only their own note. Notice where the half steps are.
steps.zh: 把音階唱上去，每位同學只唱自己的那個音。注意半音在哪裡。

steps.en: Now ask the group to start on G. Who needs to change? (Hint: one student has to become F♯.)
steps.zh: 再請大家改從 G 開始。誰要換？（提示：有一位同學必須變成 F♯。）

activities.tip_en: Let students step forward as they sing, and take the half steps as smaller steps. Then the pattern can be seen and felt.
activities.tip_zh: 讓同學唱的時候往前一步，半音的地方走小一點的步子。這樣圖樣看得見，也感覺得到。

materials.en: A tune the class knows well, written as numbers (for example 1 2 3 1 / 1 2 3 1)
materials.zh: 全班都熟的一首短曲子，用數字寫（例如 1 2 3 1 / 1 2 3 1）

materials.en: Pencils and paper
A keyboard or this page

steps.en: Write the tune as scale numbers. Play it in a major scale.
steps.zh: 把曲子寫成音階的數字。用大調音階演奏。

steps.en: Lower the third note by a half step and play it again. Does it sound different? How would you describe the change?
steps.zh: 把第三個音降低一個半音再彈一次。聽起來不一樣嗎？你會怎麼形容這個改變？

steps.en: Try the pentatonic scale by skipping the fourth and seventh notes of the major scale.
steps.zh: 試試五聲音階：跳過大調音階的第四和第七個音。

steps.en: Talk it over: what words did different students use? Is there a right answer?
steps.zh: 討論一下：不同同學用了哪些詞？有標準答案嗎？

activities.tip_en: Accept every honest description. Listeners often hear a scale differently, and that is part of what the activity shows.
activities.tip_zh: 每個誠實的形容都接受。不同的人聽音階的感覺常常不一樣，這也是這個活動要呈現的。

links_head.en: Before, around, and after this lesson
links_head.zh: 這一課的前面、旁邊和後面

links.en: How Long Is a Note?
links.note_en: Last time was about how long. This time is about how high, one step at a time.
links.note_zh: 上一課說多長；這一課說多高，一步一步地走。

links.en: How Do You Read Music?
links.note_en: The scales on this page are written on the staff you learned there.
links.note_zh: 本頁的音階，就寫在那一課學的五線譜上。

links.en: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
links.zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
links.note_en: Where the half step, 2 to the power of 1/12, comes from.
links.note_zh: 半音（2 的 1/12 次方）是怎麼來的。

links.en: Why Do Some Notes Sound Good Together?
links.zh: 為什麼有些音放在一起很好聽？
links.note_en: Next: two notes at the same time, and the simple ratios behind them.
links.note_zh: 接下來：兩個音同時響，和它們背後的簡單比例。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The scales are computed by the page itself and covered by automatic tests; the staff drawings are our own simplified shapes.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；音階由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試；五線譜上的圖形是我們自己畫的簡化圖形。

sources.en: Scale: a series of notes between one note and its octave; the first degree is the tonic; the word comes from Latin scala, ladder; W stands for a whole step of two semitones; major pattern W–W–H–W–W–W–H
sources.zh: 音階：從一個音到它的八度之間的一串音；第一級是主音；字源是拉丁文 scala（梯子）；W 是兩個半音的全音；大調圖樣 W–W–H–W–W–W–H

sources.en: Major scale: pattern W-W-H-W-W-W-H
sources.zh: 大調音階的圖樣

sources.en: Semitone (half step); a whole tone is two semitones; 12-tone equal temperament semitone ratio is the twelfth root of two (100 cents)
sources.zh: 半音；全音是兩個半音；十二平均律的半音頻率比是 2 的十二次方根（100 音分）

sources.en: Equal temperament: major scale degrees at 0, 200, 400, 500, 700, 900, 1100, 1200 cents
sources.zh: 十二平均律：大調音階各級的音分

sources.en: Natural minor scale (Aeolian) W–H–W–W–H–W–W; it can be played on the white keys A–G; major and natural minor have two semitones and five whole tones
sources.zh: 自然小調（伊奧利亞）W–H–W–W–H–W–W；可以用白鍵 A 到 G 彈出；大調與自然小調都有兩個半音和五個全音

sources.en: Pentatonic scale: five notes per octave; major pentatonic uses scale tones 1, 2, 3, 5, 6; the black keys comprise an F♯ major pentatonic scale; developed independently by many ancient civilizations; “Amazing Grace”
sources.zh: 五聲音階：每個八度五個音；大調五聲音階用大調的第 1、2、3、5、6 音；黑鍵組成 F♯ 大調五聲音階；許多古老文明各自發展；〈Amazing Grace〉

sources.en: “Auld Lang Syne”: the tune is a pentatonic Scots folk melody
sources.zh: 〈Auld Lang Syne〉：曲調是蘇格蘭民謠的五聲音階旋律

sources.en: “Mo Li Hua” uses the five-note (pentatonic) scale ubiquitous in Chinese music
sources.zh: 〈茉莉花〉用的是中國音樂裡很常見的五個音的音階

sources.en: Major and minor: minor scales tend to sound serious or melancholic to contemporary Western ears
sources.zh: 大調與小調：對當代西方人的耳朵，小調傾向聽起來嚴肅或憂傷

sources.en: Music and emotion: major–minor and positive–negative association; cross-cultural studies suggest it is probably learned
sources.zh: 音樂與情緒：大小調與正負情緒的連結；跨文化研究認為這種連結很可能是學來的

sources.en: The association between major/minor tonality and positive/negative emotional valence is psychologically robust, but without a single accepted explanation
sources.zh: 大小調與正負情緒的連結在心理學上很穩固，但沒有單一被接受的解釋

sources.en: Solfège: movable do, with do always the first degree of the major scale; fixed do
sources.zh: 唱名：首調唱名中 do 永遠是大調音階的第一級；固定唱名

sources.en: 音階: an arrangement of notes in order of pitch from a base note, a translation of scale; commonly major and minor scales and the pentatonic scale
sources.zh: 音階：以一音為基音，依高低次序排列的音列；英語 scale 的意譯；常見的有大、小調音階與五聲音階
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「音階」

sources.en: 大音階: apart from the half steps between the third and fourth and the seventh and eighth notes, all steps are whole steps
sources.zh: 大音階：除第三、四音之間，第七、八音之間為半音外，其餘皆為全音
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「大音階」

sources.en: 半音: the interval of a minor second, one twelfth of an octave; 全音: two half steps
sources.zh: 半音：小二度音程，八度音階的十二分之一；全音：兩個半音
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「半音」「全音」

sources.en: 五音: the five tones 宮、商、角、徵、羽 of ancient Chinese music, also called 五聲
sources.zh: 五音：中國古代音樂的宮、商、角、徵、羽，也稱五聲
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「五音」

sources.en: 五聲音階: each of the five tones can be the tonic, giving five pentatonic modes
sources.zh: 五聲音階：每一個音都可以當主音，形成五種不同的五聲調式
sources.src: 教育百科〈五聲音階〉（國教院《舞蹈辭典》）

sources.en: 三分損益法: remove or add a third of a length; 81 → 54 → 72; first recorded in the Guanzi and the Lüshi Chunqiu; mathematically equivalent to the Pythagorean method
sources.zh: 三分損益法：減去或加上長度的三分之一；81 → 54 → 72；最早記載於《管子》與《呂氏春秋》；在數理上與畢達哥拉斯的方法相通

sources.en: 大調: the color of a major key is usually brighter than that of a minor key
sources.zh: 大調：大調的色彩通常比小調明朗
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「大調」

sources.zh: 中文名稱：scale 音階、tonic 主音、major scale 大音階、minor scale 小音階、pentatonic scale 五聲音階、whole tone 全音、semitone 半音、mode 調式

lessons.title: Why Do Some Notes Sound Good Together?
lessons.title_zh: 為什麼有些音放在一起很好聽？
lessons.blurb_en: Play two notes at once and see their waves line up. Hear the beats when two notes are almost the same, and build major and minor chords with three keys.
lessons.blurb_zh: 讓兩個音同時響，看它們的波怎麼對齊。聽兩個幾乎相同的音發出的拍音，再用三個鍵組出大三和弦與小三和弦。
lessons.big_idea_en: When two notes sound together, a simple frequency ratio makes the combined wave repeat quickly, and many listeners hear that as blended. Notes that are almost, but not exactly, the same make beats. Three notes stacked in thirds make a chord.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 兩個音同時響時，簡單的頻率比會讓疊起來的波很快重複，許多人聽起來就覺得融在一起。幾乎相同、但不完全相同的音會產生拍音。三個音按三度疊起來，就是和弦。

lab.how_en: The lower note is always 220 Hz. Choose an interval, then press “Together” to hear both notes at once. The top wave is the lower note, the middle one is the upper note, and the bottom one is what you get when they are added together. Dashed lines mark where the combined wave starts to repeat. Then move the slider to mistune the upper note, and watch the loudness rise and fall: those are beats.
lab.how_zh: 下面的音一律是 220 赫茲。選一個音程，再按「一起響」同時聽兩個音。最上面的波是低音，中間是高音，最下面是兩者疊在一起的結果。虛線標出疊起來的波從哪裡開始重複。再移動滑桿，把高音調歪，看音量一起一伏：那就是拍音。

paras: An interval is the difference in pitch between two sounds. You can also say it as a frequency ratio. Two notes an octave apart have a ratio of 2 to 1. A perfect fifth is 3 to 2, a perfect fourth is 4 to 3, a major third is 5 to 4, and a minor third is 6 to 5. You met 2 to 1 and 3 to 2 on the string in lesson 1.

An interval’s name counts the notes it covers, with both ends included. From C to E is a third, because C, D, and E are three notes. In semitones, a minor third is 3, a major third is 4, a perfect fourth is 5, and a perfect fifth is 7. A perfect fifth is at the start of “Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.” A piano is not exactly in these ratios: its fifth is 700 cents, but 3 to 2 is about 701.96 cents, and its major third is about 14 cents wider than 5 to 4.

Musicians call a stable combination of notes a consonance, a point of rest. They call a tense combination a dissonance, which seems to want to move on. Consonance is often associated with simple ratios. Look at the lab: when two notes are an octave apart, the combined wave repeats as fast as the lower note. For a fifth it lines up again every 1/110 of a second. For a half step the pattern takes much longer, and the two notes seem to rub against each other.

When two notes are almost the same, you hear something else. The sound gets louder and softer, again and again, and this is called beats. The beat rate is the difference between the two frequencies: 220 Hz and 224 Hz make 4 beats per second. Slow beats are heard as the loudness changing, and faster ones, above about 20 per second, as a rough, fluttering sound. Piano tuners listen for beats to know when two strings are in tune. These beats are not the beat of a song, which you learned about in lesson 3.

A chord is two or more notes sounding at the same time. A triad has three notes stacked in thirds: the root, then a third above, then a fifth above. A major triad is a major third and a perfect fifth above the root, so from C it is C, E, G. In just intonation its ratio is 4 : 5 : 6. A minor triad has a minor third instead, so from C it is C, E♭, G. Only the middle note is different, by one half step. Major and minor triads are the most common triads in Western music.

Is the pleasure of consonance built in, or learned? Researchers still debate it. In a 2016 study, people of the Tsimane’, an Amazonian society with little exposure to Western music, rated consonant and dissonant chords as equally pleasant. But they still disliked rough sounds. Dissonance is not simply bad, either. Dissonances often play a decisive role in making music pleasant. So listen with open ears, and let your own listening tell you what you find beautiful.
paras_zh: 音程是兩個聲音之間音高的差距。你也可以用頻率比來說：差一個八度的兩個音，頻率比是 2 比 1；完全五度是 3 比 2，完全四度是 4 比 3，大三度是 5 比 4，小三度是 6 比 5。2 比 1 和 3 比 2，你在第一課的弦上就遇到過。
音程的名字是數它涵蓋的音，頭尾都算。C 到 E 是三度，因為 C、D、E 是三個音。用半音數來說：小三度是 3、大三度是 4、完全四度是 5、完全五度是 7。〈小星星〉一開始就是完全五度。鋼琴並不完全照這些比例：它的五度是 700 音分，而 3 比 2 約是 701.96 音分；它的大三度比 5 比 4 寬約 14 音分。
音樂家把穩定的音的組合叫協和，是休息、到達的地方；把緊張的組合叫不協和，好像想要往前走。協和常常和簡單的比連在一起。看看實驗室：兩個音差八度時，疊起來的波重複得和低音一樣快；五度每 1/110 秒重新對齊一次；半音的圖樣要花久得多，兩個音聽起來好像在彼此摩擦。
當兩個音幾乎相同時，你會聽到另一種現象：聲音一次又一次地變大、變小，這叫拍音。拍音的速度就是兩個頻率的差：220 赫茲和 224 赫茲會產生每秒 4 次的拍音。慢的拍音聽起來是音量在變；每秒超過約 20 次，就變成粗糙、顫動的聲音。調琴師聽拍音來判斷兩條弦準不準。這裡的拍音，和你在第三課學的歌曲的「拍」不是同一件事。
和弦是兩個或更多的音同時響。三和弦有三個音，按三度疊起來：根音、上面的三度音、再上面的五度音。大三和弦是根音上面有大三度和完全五度，從 C 開始就是 C、E、G；在純律裡它的比是 4 : 5 : 6。小三和弦用小三度，從 C 開始是 C、E♭、G。只有中間的音不同，差一個半音。大三和弦與小三和弦是西方音樂裡最常用的三和弦。
協和的愉悅是天生的，還是學來的？研究者還在爭論。2016 年的一項研究裡，奇曼內人（Tsimane’，亞馬遜雨林裡很少接觸西方音樂的社群）認為協和與不協和的和弦同樣悅耳；但他們還是不喜歡粗糙的聲音。不協和也不只是「不好」：不協和常常是讓音樂變得悅耳的關鍵。所以請用開放的耳朵去聽，讓你自己的聆聽告訴你，你覺得什麼美。
questions: Why is the interval from C to E called a third?
What do you hear when you play 220 Hz and 224 Hz together, and how fast is it?
What is the difference between a major triad and a minor triad?
answers: Because the name counts the notes it covers, with both ends included: C, D, E are three notes.
You hear beats, the loudness rising and falling. The rate is the difference between the frequencies, 224 − 220 = 4 times per second.
Only the middle note. A major triad has a major third (4 semitones) above the root, and a minor triad has a minor third (3 semitones). Both have a perfect fifth (7 semitones).

vocab.ex: The interval between C and G is a fifth.
vocab.exzh: C 和 G 之間的音程是五度。

vocab.ex: An octave has a frequency ratio of 2 to 1.
vocab.exzh: 八度的頻率比是 2 比 1。

vocab.ex: A perfect fifth has a ratio of 3 to 2.
vocab.exzh: 純五度的比是 3 比 2。

vocab.ex: Many people hear a perfect fifth as consonant.
vocab.exzh: 許多人聽純五度覺得協和。

vocab.ex: A dissonant interval sounds tense and wants to move.
vocab.exzh: 不協和的音程聽起來緊張，好像想要走開。

vocab.ex: A chord is three or more notes played together.
vocab.exzh: 和弦是三個或更多的音一起彈。

vocab.ex: A triad has three notes: a root, a third, and a fifth.
vocab.exzh: 三和弦有三個音：根音、三度音、五度音。

vocab.ex: Two strings that are almost in tune make slow beats.
vocab.exzh: 兩條幾乎準了的弦會發出緩慢的拍音。

quiz.q: What is the frequency ratio of a perfect fifth, in the simple (just) form?
How many semitones are in a major third?
What do you hear when two notes are almost, but not exactly, the same frequency?
options: Beats: the loudness rises and falls

quiz.q: How does a minor triad differ from a major triad?
options: The middle note is one half step lower
The top note is an octave higher

quiz.q: A C major triad is C E G. How many semitones is G above C?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_en: The simplest ratio after the unison
parts.text_en: The combined wave repeats 220 times a second, as fast as the lower note itself.
parts.text_zh: 疊起來的波每秒重複 220 次，和低音本身一樣快。

parts.meta_en: The ratio you met on the string in lesson 1
parts.meta_zh: 第一課在弦上遇過的比
parts.text_en: Two waves line up again every 1/110 of a second. Look at the dashed lines.
parts.text_zh: 兩個波每 1/110 秒重新對齊一次。看看虛線。

parts.meta_en: Minor second, a half step apart
parts.text_en: The pattern repeats only about 15 times a second, and the two notes rub against each other.
parts.text_zh: 圖樣每秒只重複約 15 次，兩個音彼此摩擦。

parts.text_en: The upper note is mistuned a little. The loudness swells and fades, again and again.
parts.text_zh: 高音被調歪了一點。音量一次又一次地變大、變小。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself: choose the unison and drag the slider slowly. When does the pulsing slow down and stop?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己試試：選同度，慢慢拖動滑桿。起伏什麼時候變慢、停下來？

chord.lead_en: Press three keys, and the page tells you what chord they make. Try C E G, then lower the E by one key. What changed?
chord.lead_zh: 按三個鍵，頁面會告訴你它們組成什麼和弦。試試 C E G，再把 E 降低一個鍵。有什麼改變？

chordq.zh: 大三和弦還是小三和弦？
chordq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays a triad. Choose major or minor. If you cannot hear the sound, press “Show the notes” and look at how far the middle note is above the lowest one.
chordq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題播放一個三和弦。選大三和弦或小三和弦。如果聽不到聲音，按「看音」，看中間的音比最低音高幾個半音。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names unison singing, rounds, part singing, and harmony. The words “interval,” “chord,” “triad,” “consonance,” and “dissonance” do not appear in the curriculum itself.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱寫到齊唱、輪唱、合唱和和聲。「音程」「和弦」「三和弦」「協和」「不協和」這些詞，課綱本文裡沒有出現。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 多元形式歌曲，如：獨唱、齊唱等。
items.note_en: In unison singing, everyone sings the same note. That is a ratio of 1 to 1.
items.note_zh: 齊唱時大家唱同一個音，頻率比是 1 比 1。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 多元形式歌曲，如：輪唱、合唱等。
items.note_en: In rounds and part singing, different notes sound together.
items.note_zh: 輪唱與合唱時，不同的音會同時響。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國中七至九年級）
items.text: 音樂元素，如：音色、調式、和聲等。
items.note_en: Harmony is first named as a musical element in junior high school.
items.note_zh: 和聲在國中才第一次被列為音樂元素。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國中七至九年級）
items.text: 相關音樂語彙，如音色、和聲等描述音樂元素之音樂術語，或相關之一般性用語。
items.note_en: Words for describing harmony are part of musical vocabulary.
items.note_zh: 描述和聲的詞彙，屬於音樂語彙。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A name, a legend, a rough sound, and different ears
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個名字、一個傳說、一種粗糙的聲音，和不同的耳朵
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people have thought about sounds that go together.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人們怎麼看待一起響的聲音的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: Perfect intervals, such as the fourth, fifth, and octave, are called perfect because they were traditionally considered perfectly consonant. Taiwan’s standard translations use the word 完全, as in 完全五度, for perfect fifth. The name does not mean that every other interval is imperfect, or that a perfect interval is always the best choice.
cards.body_zh: 完全音程，例如四度、五度和八度，叫「完全」，是因為傳統上它們被認為是完全協和的。台灣的標準譯名用「完全」兩個字，例如 perfect fifth 是完全五度。這個名字不表示其他音程就是不完美，也不表示完全音程永遠是最好的選擇。

cards.body_en: According to legend, Pythagoras heard blacksmiths’ hammers ringing and discovered that musical notes could be turned into numbers. But no authentic writings of Pythagoras survive, and modern scholars usually ascribe these discoveries to the later Pythagorean Philolaus. The tuning built from fifths is named after Pythagoras, but its system dates back to ancient Mesopotamia.
cards.body_zh: 依傳說，畢達哥拉斯聽到鐵匠的錘子敲擊聲，發現音可以變成數字。但畢達哥拉斯本人沒有留下可靠的著作，現代學者通常把這些發現歸給後來的畢達哥拉斯學派的菲洛勞斯。用五度疊出來的音律以畢達哥拉斯命名，但這個系統可以追溯到古代美索不達米亞。

cards.k: A Rough Sound · 粗糙的聲音
cards.body_en: Beats are not always a mistake. Many pipe organs have “celeste” stops that intentionally produce beating, and in some musical traditions people consider the rough, fluttering sound an attractive part of the timbre. Whether a sound is pleasant depends on the style of music and the listener.
cards.body_zh: 拍音不一定是錯誤。許多管風琴有「天使音栓」（celeste），故意製造拍音；有些音樂傳統認為，這種粗糙、顫動的聲音是迷人的音色的一部分。一個聲音好不好聽，要看音樂的風格與聽的人。

cards.body_en: In a 2016 study published in Nature, the Tsimane’, a native Amazonian society with minimal exposure to Western culture, rated consonant and dissonant chords and vocal harmonies as equally pleasant. They did show Western-like dislike for acoustic roughness. Bolivian town and city dwellers preferred consonance, less strongly than US residents did. The authors concluded that culture has a dominant role in shaping these responses, and other researchers still argue for a biological part.
cards.body_zh: 2016 年發表在《自然》期刊的一項研究中，奇曼內人（Tsimane’，亞馬遜地區、很少接觸西方文化的原住民社群）認為協和與不協和的和弦與人聲和聲同樣悅耳；但他們和西方人一樣不喜歡粗糙的聲音。玻利維亞城鎮的居民比較喜歡協和，程度比美國居民輕。作者的結論是文化在塑造這些反應上占主導地位；也有其他研究者主張其中有生物性的成分。

myths.myth_en: Dissonant means bad.
myths.myth_zh: 不協和就是不好聽。
myths.fact_en: A dissonance is a tension that wants to move on. Dissonances often play a decisive role in making music pleasant.
myths.fact_zh: 不協和是一種想要往前走的緊張。不協和常常是讓音樂悅耳的關鍵。

myths.myth_en: A piano plays exactly 3 to 2 for a fifth.
myths.myth_zh: 鋼琴彈出的五度就是剛好 3 比 2。
myths.fact_en: A piano’s fifth is 700 cents, and 3 to 2 is about 701.96 cents. It is very close, but not the same. Its major third is about 14 cents wider than 5 to 4.
myths.fact_zh: 鋼琴的五度是 700 音分，3 比 2 約是 701.96 音分，非常接近，但不完全一樣。它的大三度比 5 比 4 寬約 14 音分。

myths.myth_en: Everyone hears consonance the same way.
myths.myth_zh: 每個人聽到的協和都一樣。
myths.fact_en: Researchers still debate how much is built in and how much is learned. One study found a group who rated consonant and dissonant chords as equally pleasant.
myths.fact_zh: 研究者還在爭論有多少是天生的、有多少是學來的。有一項研究發現，有一個社群認為協和與不協和的和弦同樣悅耳。

myths.myth_en: Pythagoras discovered the ratios from blacksmiths’ hammers.
myths.myth_zh: 畢達哥拉斯是聽鐵錘發現比例的。
myths.fact_en: That is a legend. No authentic writings of Pythagoras survive, and scholars usually ascribe the discoveries to Philolaus.
myths.fact_zh: 那是傳說。畢達哥拉斯沒有留下可靠的著作，學者通常把這些發現歸給菲洛勞斯。

tricks.body_en: 2:1, 3:2, 4:3: the combined wave lines up often.
tricks.body_zh: 2:1、3:2、4:3：疊起來的波常常對齊。

tricks.body_en: The beat rate is the difference in frequency.
tricks.body_zh: 拍音的速度就是頻率的差。

tricks.body_en: C E G: stack every other note of the scale.
tricks.body_zh: C E G：每隔一個音疊一個。

tricks.body_en: Count the half steps from the root.
tricks.body_zh: 從根音開始數半音。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. When two or three notes sound together, the total is louder than one note, so be careful.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。兩三個音一起響時，總音量比一個音大，要特別小心。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: The rough, beating sounds on this page are not harmful at a low volume, but if a sound bothers you, stop it. You do not have to listen to a sound that feels unpleasant.
safety.zh: 本頁粗糙、起伏的聲音在小音量下沒有害處；但如果某個聲音讓你不舒服，就停下來。你不必勉強聽讓你不舒服的聲音。

materials.en: Pairs of students
A keyboard or this page to give the starting note
materials.zh: 鍵盤或本頁，用來給起始音

steps.en: Both students sing the same comfortable note together, as steady as they can.
steps.zh: 兩位同學一起唱同一個舒服的音，盡量穩。

steps.en: One student slowly slides the pitch a tiny bit higher, then back. Everyone listens for the pulsing, which is beats.
steps.zh: 其中一位慢慢把音高滑高一點點，再滑回來。大家聽那種一起一伏，就是拍音。

steps.en: Find the exact moment when the pulsing disappears. That is when the two notes match.
steps.zh: 找到起伏消失的那一刻。那就是兩個音對上的時候。

steps.en: Now try to sing a fifth apart. One student holds the note while the other finds the note that sounds blended.
steps.zh: 再試試相差五度。一位同學唱住音，另一位找出聽起來融在一起的音。

activities.tip_en: Singing in tune with another voice is hard at first, so let students try several times and praise the effort. Stay in a comfortable range.
activities.tip_zh: 一開始要和別人唱得準很難，讓同學多試幾次，肯定他們的努力。待在舒服的音域裡。

materials.en: A keyboard or this page
Paper and pencils

steps.en: Play a major triad and a minor triad on the same root, one after the other. Write down words that describe each one.
steps.zh: 在同一個根音上，先後彈一個大三和弦和一個小三和弦。把形容它們的詞寫下來。

steps.en: Count the half steps from the lowest note to the middle note. Write 4 or 3 next to each word list.
steps.zh: 數最低音到中間音有幾個半音。在每份詞彙旁寫下 4 或 3。

steps.en: Move both chords to a new root and play them again. Do the words still fit?
steps.zh: 把兩個和弦移到新的根音再彈一次。這些詞還適用嗎？

steps.en: Share your lists. Did everybody pick the same words? Why might people differ?
steps.zh: 分享你們的詞彙。每個人選的詞一樣嗎？為什麼人們可能不一樣？

activities.tip_en: Accept every honest description. The activity is not a test of the “right” feeling.
activities.tip_zh: 每個誠實的形容都接受。這個活動不是在測驗「標準」的感覺。

links_head.en: Before, around, and after this lesson
links_head.zh: 這一課的前面、旁邊和後面

links.en: What Is a Scale?
links.note_en: The three notes of a major triad are the first, third, and fifth notes of a major scale.
links.note_zh: 大三和弦的三個音，是大調音階的第一、三、五個音。

links.en: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
links.zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
links.note_en: Where the ratios 2 to 1 and 3 to 2 first appeared, on a string.
links.note_zh: 2 比 1 和 3 比 2 第一次出現的地方：一條弦。

links.en: Why Does a Piano Sound Different from a Violin?
links.zh: 同一個音，鋼琴和小提琴為什麼聽起來不一樣？
links.note_en: Harmonics are the reason a note and its octave share partials.
links.note_zh: 諧波，就是一個音與它的八度共用泛音的原因。

links.en: How Do Instruments Make Sound?
links.note_en: Next: the four kinds of things that vibrate to make a sound.
links.note_zh: 接下來：四種會振動、發出聲音的東西。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The waves, ratios, and chords are computed by the page itself and covered by automatic tests.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；波形、比例與和弦由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試。

sources.en: An interval is a difference in pitch between two sounds; frequency ratios 2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, 6:5; interval numbers count scale degrees with both ends; perfect intervals were traditionally considered perfectly consonant; Helmholtz theorized that dissonance was caused by beats
sources.zh: 音程是兩個聲音的音高差；頻率比 2:1、3:2、4:3、5:4、6:5；音程的度數頭尾都算；完全音程傳統上被認為完全協和；亥姆霍茲認為不協和來自拍音

sources.en: Seven semitones in equal temperament; a frequency ratio of 3:2, or very nearly so; at the start of “Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star”; more consonant than any interval except the unison and the octave
sources.zh: 平均律中是七個半音；頻率比 3:2 或非常接近；〈小星星〉一開始；除了同度和八度，比其他音程都更協和

sources.en: Four half steps; 5:4 is 386.31 cents; 13.69 cents narrower than the equal-tempered major third
sources.zh: 四個半音；5:4 是 386.31 音分；平均律的大三度比它寬 13.69 音分

sources.en: A stable tone combination is a consonance; consonance is often associated with simple ratios; partials of the higher octave note are partials of the lower; beating and roughness; dissonances often play a decisive role in making music pleasant; varies across cultures and styles
sources.zh: 穩定的音組合是協和；協和常和簡單的比連在一起；高八度音的泛音也是低音的泛音；拍音與粗糙感；不協和常是讓音樂悅耳的關鍵；因文化與風格而異

sources.en: Interference between two sounds of slightly different frequencies, perceived as a periodic variation in volume, the rate of which is the difference of the two frequencies; tuning by beats; organ celeste stops
sources.zh: 兩個頻率略有不同的聲音的干涉，聽起來是音量週期性變化，速度是兩個頻率的差；用拍音調音；管風琴的天使音栓

sources.en: Equal-tempered fifth 700 cents vs 701.96; major third 400 vs 386.31; minor third 300 vs 315.64; fifths and fourths almost indistinguishably close to just intervals
sources.zh: 平均律五度 700 音分對 701.96；大三度 400 對 386.31；小三度 300 對 315.64；五度與四度幾乎和純律分辨不出來

sources.en: A chord is two or more notes at the same time; a triad is three notes stacked in thirds; major and minor triads are the most commonly used
sources.zh: 和弦是兩個或更多的音同時響；三和弦是三個音按三度疊起；大、小三和弦最常用

sources.en: Major triad: major third and perfect fifth above the root, {0,4,7}, just ratio 4:5:6; minor triad {0,3,7}, 10:12:15
sources.zh: 大三和弦：根音上有大三度與完全五度，{0,4,7}，純律比 4:5:6；小三和弦 {0,3,7}，10:12:15

sources.en: According to legend; no authentic writings survive; discoveries ascribed to Philolaus; the tuning system dates back to ancient Mesopotamia
sources.zh: 據說；沒有可靠的著作留存；發現歸給菲洛勞斯；這個音律可追溯到古代美索不達米亞

sources.en: The Tsimane’ rated consonant and dissonant chords and vocal harmonies as equally pleasant; Western-like responses to acoustic roughness; culture has a dominant role
sources.zh: 奇曼內人認為協和與不協和的和弦與人聲和聲同樣悅耳；對粗糙聲音有類似西方的反應；文化占主導地位

sources.en: Reviews mathematical, physical, and biological explanations of consonance; argues that a biological explanation is plausible
sources.zh: 回顧協和的數學、物理與生物解釋；主張生物解釋是可能的

sources.en: 音程: the difference in pitch between two notes, counted in 度; 八度音程: the vibration frequencies differ by a factor of two
sources.zh: 音程：兩音之間的音高差距，以度計算；八度音程：振動頻率相差一倍

sources.en: When two sound waves of nearly the same frequency combine, a sound that alternates strong and weak is heard, called 拍音

units.blurb_en: Strings, air, skins, and boards: the four kinds of things that vibrate, and how a piano, an orchestra, and Chinese instruments put them to work.
units.blurb_zh: 弦、空氣、膜和板：四種會振動的東西，以及鋼琴、交響樂團和國樂器怎麼運用它們。

lessons.title: How Do Instruments Make Sound?
lessons.blurb_en: Four stands, four families: a string, a column of air, a drumhead, and a bar. Click each one to hear it, watch what vibrates, and find out how each family goes higher.
lessons.blurb_zh: 四個展示台，四個家族：弦、空氣柱、鼓膜和一根棒。一個一個點，聽聲音、看是什麼在振動，再找出每一家怎麼變高。
lessons.big_idea_en: Every instrument sounds because something vibrates. We group instruments by what vibrates: a string, a column of air, a membrane, or the body of the instrument itself.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 每一種樂器會發聲，都是因為有東西在振動。我們依「是什麼在振動」把樂器分組：弦、空氣柱、膜，或樂器本身。

lab.how_en: From left to right: a string on a box, a tube of air closed at the bottom, a drum, and a bar. Click a stand to hear that family and see what vibrates. On the string, you see the string shake in halves and thirds at once. In the tube, the little dots are air, moving back and forth. On the drum, the head swells up and down in two patterns together. The bar bends, with its ends and its middle moving in opposite directions. The motion is slowed down on purpose, and our sounds are simple recipes, not recordings.
lab.how_zh: 由左到右：箱子上的一條弦、下面封閉的一管空氣、一面鼓、一根棒。點一個展示台，聽那一家的聲音，看是什麼在振動。弦會同時以一半、三分之一的方式振動；管子裡的小點是空氣，前後晃動；鼓皮同時以兩種圖樣一起一伏；棒會彎曲，兩端和中間的動向相反。振動畫面是刻意放慢的，我們的聲音是簡單的配方，不是錄音。

legend.en: Click a stand: it sounds and moves
legend.zh: 點展示台：發聲，並且動起來

legend.en: Each family has its own list of overtones
legend.zh: 每一家有自己的一組泛音

lab.scale_en: The vibrations are slowed down: the lowest tone shakes about once a second here. The ratios between the overtones are the real ones.
lab.scale_zh: 振動是放慢的：最低的音在這裡每秒約振動一次。泛音之間的比例是真的。
lab.credit_html: All sounds on this page are made by your browser, tone by tone. They are simple recipes for each family, not recordings of real instruments. · 本頁所有的聲音都由瀏覽器即時合成，是每一家的簡單配方，不是真樂器的錄音。

paras: Every sound starts with something that vibrates. Musical instruments can be grouped by what it is. A well-known system was devised by Erich von Hornbostel and Curt Sachs and published in 1914. It uses four families: chordophones, where a string vibrates; aerophones, where air vibrates; membranophones, where a stretched membrane vibrates; and idiophones, where the body of the instrument itself vibrates. In Taiwan they are 弦鳴樂器, 氣鳴樂器, 膜鳴樂器, and 體鳴樂器.

A string’s pitch depends on three things. The shorter the string, the higher the pitch. The tighter the string, the higher the pitch. And the lighter the string, the higher the pitch. A string alone barely moves the air, so most string instruments have a body. The soundboard moves a greater volume of air than the thin string, and that makes the sound louder. The body does not add energy. The string is still where the sound comes from. Strings can be plucked, bowed, or struck.

In a wind instrument the air inside a tube vibrates, and the player starts it in one of three ways: by blowing across an edge, as in a flute, by making a reed vibrate, as in a clarinet, or by buzzing the lips, as in a trumpet. The pitch depends on the length of the tube. Finger holes, valves, and slides change the effective length. A tube that is closed at one end makes only the odd harmonics, 1, 3, 5, and so on, and sounds an octave lower than an open tube of the same length. A clarinet behaves roughly like that, and a flute behaves like an open tube.

A drum has a stretched membrane. When you tighten the head, the pitch goes up. A circular membrane does not vibrate in whole-number multiples. For an ideal drumhead the overtones are about 1.59, 2.14, 2.30, and 2.92 times the lowest frequency. That makes a drum sound different from a string, and many drums have no clear pitch. But some, such as the timpani, are tuned to definite pitches with a pedal that changes the tension of the head.

In a marimba or a xylophone, the bar itself vibrates. A free bar has overtones at about 2.76, 5.40, and 8.93 times its lowest frequency, which are not whole numbers either. Makers tune a marimba bar by taking wood from the middle of its underside, which lowers the pitch. The shorter the bar, the higher the pitch. A bell is a body too. A well-tuned bell has a hum, a strike tone, a tierce, a quint, and a nominal.

So the family is not about the material. A saxophone is usually made of brass, but it is a woodwind, because a reed starts the vibration. Our ears also use more than the overtones to tell instruments apart. Researchers say the timbre depends mainly on the frequency spectrum, but also on the attack and on how the sound changes in time. The sounds on this page are our own simple recipes, so real instruments sound richer.
paras_zh: 每個聲音都始於某個東西在振動。樂器可以依「是什麼在振動」來分組。有一套著名的系統，由霍恩博斯特爾（Erich von Hornbostel）和薩克斯（Curt Sachs）提出，1914 年發表。它分成四個家族：弦鳴樂器，是弦在振動；氣鳴樂器，是空氣在振動；膜鳴樂器，是拉緊的膜在振動；體鳴樂器，是樂器本身在振動。在台灣的標準譯名是弦鳴樂器、氣鳴樂器、膜鳴樂器和體鳴樂器。
弦的音高取決於三件事：弦越短，音越高；弦越緊，音越高；弦越輕，音越高。弦自己幾乎推不動空氣，所以大多數弦樂器有琴身。共鳴板比細細的弦推動更多的空氣，聲音就變大聲。琴身不會增加能量；聲音的來源還是弦。弦可以撥、可以用弓拉，也可以敲。
管樂器是管子裡的空氣在振動，演奏者用三種方式讓它開始：吹過邊緣，如長笛；讓簧片振動，如單簧管；或用嘴唇嗡嗡振動，如小號。音高取決於管子的長度，按音孔、活塞和滑管會改變有效長度。一端封閉的管子只有奇數諧波 1、3、5……，基音比同長度的開管低一個八度。單簧管大致像這樣；長笛則像開管。
鼓有一張拉緊的膜。把鼓皮拉緊，音就變高。圓形的膜不是整數倍地振動：理想鼓皮的泛音大約是最低頻率的 1.59、2.14、2.30、2.92 倍。這讓鼓聽起來和弦不同，許多鼓沒有明確的音高。不過有些鼓，例如定音鼓，用踏板改變鼓皮的張力，可以調到確定的音高。
在馬林巴琴或木琴裡，是琴鍵那根棒本身在振動。兩端自由的棒，泛音大約是最低頻率的 2.76、5.40、8.93 倍，也不是整數倍。製作者調馬林巴琴鍵的音，是從琴鍵底面中間削掉木頭，音會變低。棒越短，音越高。鐘也是體鳴樂器。調好音的鐘有低音（hum）、敲擊音（strike）、小三度音（tierce）、五度音（quint）和高八度音（nominal）。
所以家族和材料沒有關係。薩克斯風通常是銅做的，但它是木管樂器，因為開始振動的是簧片。我們的耳朵也不只靠泛音來分辨樂器。研究者說，音色主要取決於頻率頻譜，但也取決於起音和聲音隨時間的變化。本頁的聲音是我們自己的簡單配方，所以真樂器聽起來更豐富。
questions: Why is a saxophone a woodwind, even though it is usually made of brass?
What happens to a string’s pitch when you make the string half as long?
What makes the overtones of a drum different from those of a string?
answers: Because a vibrating reed starts the sound. The family depends on how the vibration is started, not on the material.
The frequency doubles, so the pitch goes up one octave. This is the 2 to 1 ratio from lesson 1.
A string’s overtones are whole-number multiples, 1, 2, 3… times the lowest. A drumhead’s overtones are not: about 1, 1.59, 2.14, 2.30, 2.92.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch the string shake as a whole and in halves and thirds at the same time.
parts.text_zh: 看弦同時整根、一半、三分之一地振動。

parts.text_en: The dots near the bottom hardly move, and the ones at the open top swing the most.
parts.text_zh: 下面的點幾乎不動，開口上面的點晃得最大。

parts.text_en: Two patterns at once: the whole head moves, and the two halves rock against each other.
parts.text_zh: 兩種圖樣同時發生：整張皮一起動，和兩半一上一下。

parts.text_en: The ends move up while the middle moves down. The two posts sit where the bar hardly moves.
parts.text_zh: 兩端往上時，中間往下。兩根支柱放在棒幾乎不動的地方。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the sliders in the next section: which family needs the biggest change to go up by an octave?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試下一節的滑桿：哪一家要改變最多，才能高一個八度？

pitchup.en: How Can You Make It Higher?
pitchup.lead_en: Each family has its own way to go higher. Move a slider and listen. The numbers come from the proportions in the notes below each card: a string and a tube go up as they get shorter, a drum as its head gets tighter, and a bar as it gets shorter. How far must each one change to go up a full octave?
pitchup.lead_zh: 每一家都有自己變高的方法。拖動滑桿，聽聽看。數字來自每張卡下面的比例關係：弦和管子越短越高，鼓皮越緊越高，棒越短越高。每一家要改變多少，才能高一個完整的八度？

famq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays a sound from one of the four families. Choose which one is vibrating. If you cannot hear the sound, press “Show the overtones”: whole numbers 1, 2, 3 are a string, odd numbers are a closed pipe, and numbers that are not whole belong to a drum, a bar, or a bell.
famq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題播放四個家族之一的聲音。選出是什麼在振動。如果聽不到聲音，按「看泛音」：整數 1、2、3 是弦，奇數是封閉的管，不是整數的是鼓、棒或鐘。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names the classification of instruments in grades 5 to 6 and how instruments make sound in junior high school. It does not use the words for the four families, or any words about vibration.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱在國小高年級寫到樂器的分類，在國中寫到樂器的發音原理。課綱本文沒有出現四個家族的名稱，也沒有「振動」這類詞。
